signals.topic: Java quickstart documentation fails to run due to missing classpath setup and incorrect Maven version reference
signals.summary: The Java Get Started page quickstart instructs users to run `javac QuickStart.java` and `java QuickStart` without providing any classpath configuration for the required `com.anthropic.*` JARs, causing compilation and execution to fail immediately. Additionally, the Maven/Gradle snippets reference version `2.20.0` which does not exist on Maven Central (latest is `2.26.0`), further blocking new users from completing the quickstart.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because it completely blocks the primary onboarding flow (Get Started) for every new Java SDK user. The missing classpath setup causes javac compilation to fail with undefined class errors, and the non-existent Maven version (2.20.0) causes dependency resolution to fail with a 404. Together these make the quickstart unusable, satisfying the '主流程失败/阻断' criterion. Evidence is explicit and reproducible.

source_issues.title: Java quickstart docs: javac/java commands don't work without classpath setup, version 2.20.0 doesn't exist
source_issues.evidence: The issue explicitly states: 'The docs tell users to run: javac QuickStart.java / java QuickStart. This fails immediately because QuickStart.java imports com.anthropic.* JARs that javac has no knowledge of.' Additionally, 'The Maven/Gradle snippets reference version 2.20.0, which returns a 404 from Maven Central.' Both issues block the new user onboarding flow entirely.

signals.topic: Streaming aggregator silently drops content blocks and metadata — breaks code_execution continuation and server tool result tracking
signals.summary: The streaming message aggregator (get_final_message()) fails to propagate multiple data elements from the SSE stream: (1) container.id from message_delta events (breaks multi-turn code_execution with container_id requirement), (2) BetaToolSearchToolResultBlock and BetaWebFetchToolResultBlock types missing from ParsedBetaContentBlock union causing silent block drops, (3) BetaInputJsonEvent not fired for server_tool_use blocks. Users either get None/missing data or silently lost content, forcing manual SSE parsing or fallback to non-streaming mode.
signals.review_reason: Three related but distinct bugs all in the streaming message aggregator layer cause data loss or unavailability in streaming mode. Issue #1424 is production-critical: container.id is None in streaming, causing 400 errors on every subsequent turn with code_execution, forcing manual SSE interception. Issues #1422 and #1421 cause silent content block drops and missing events. Together they represent a systemic streaming aggregator gap that breaks multi-turn tool loops and server tool result delivery — core streaming use cases.

source_issues.title: `get_final_message()` does not propagate `message_delta.container` into aggregated Message (breaks code_execution continuation)
source_issues.evidence: stream.get_final_message().container returns None in streaming mode; non-streaming messages.create() returns container correctly. Subsequent API calls fail with 400 'container_id is required'. Production code forced to manually subscribe to RawMessageDeltaEvent to extract container.id.

source_issues.title: ParsedBetaContentBlock union missing tool_search/web_fetch result blocks — stream accumulator drops them from get_final_message()
source_issues.evidence: BetaToolSearchToolResultBlock and BetaWebFetchToolResultBlock are absent from ParsedBetaContentBlock union. Streaming accumulator silently drops these blocks; get_final_message().content is missing tool result blocks that were present on the wire.

source_issues.title: BetaInputJsonEvent not fired for server_tool_use blocks during streaming
source_issues.evidence: SDK correctly accumulates streamed server tool input into content_block.input but never fires BetaInputJsonEvent to consumers. No parsed event emitted for server_tool_use input streaming; workaround requires matching on raw BetaRawContentBlockDeltaEvent.

signals.topic: Batch API intermittent 404 errors crash production applications — server-side propagation delay causes NotFoundError on create/retrieve/results
signals.summary: After successfully creating a message batch, subsequent calls to batches.retrieve() and batches.results() intermittently return 404 Not Found due to transient server-side infrastructure propagation delay. Cases include: (1) retrieve() returns 404 seconds after creation, (2) results() crashes the application when it internally calls retrieve() and gets 404, (3) even batches.create() itself returns 404. All affected batches eventually completed successfully but the intermittent 404s crash callers that don't catch NotFoundError.
signals.review_reason: Despite count=1, this is a genuine production-blocking issue. The application crashes when batches.results() encounters a 404 because its internal retrieve() call fails. The issue provides detailed production logs, full traceback showing app crash, and three failure modes within a single window. The crash is deterministic when the propagation delay hits at the wrong moment, making this a reliability blocker for any production batch workload.

source_issues.title: Intermittent `NotFoundError (404)` on Batch API — server-side propagation delay
source_issues.evidence: Production application crashed: batches.results() triggers internal retrieve() which returns 404 Not Found, raising NotFoundError that propagates to crash the app. Three distinct failure modes observed in same 15-minute window. Workaround requires catching NotFoundError and falling back to messages.create().

signals.topic: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with Apify and other Streamable HTTP-only MCP servers
signals.summary: The Managed Agents API (client.beta.agents / sessions) connects to MCP servers using SSE transport only. Apify deprecated their SSE endpoint on April 1, 2026 and now only supports Streamable HTTP, causing all Managed Agents sessions with Apify MCP server to fail at initialization with 'MCP server apify initialize failed: SSE data line is not valid JSON'. No workaround available; Apify is completely unusable with Managed Agents.
signals.review_reason: This is a breaking compatibility issue: a major MCP provider (Apify) dropped SSE support and now only serves Streamable HTTP, making the entire Managed Agents MCP integration unusable with Apify from the date of their deprecation. The user impact is total service unavailability for that integration path, with no workaround available. This qualifies as a functional blocker despite single-count because it's an external service breaking change with zero client-side mitigation.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with servers that have dropped SSE (e.g. Apify)
source_issues.evidence: Apify deprecated SSE endpoint on 2026-04-01. Any Managed Agents session using Apify MCP server now fails with 'SSE data line is not valid JSON'. Agent falls back to other tools and never uses Apify. No client-side workaround available; Apify is completely unusable.

signals.topic: container_upload block silently ignored when no active container exists — data loss with no error or warning
signals.summary: When a container_upload block is included in a message payload with no active container, the API silently ignores it: no error is raised, no warning is returned, the file is simply never mounted. This silent success makes it impossible to reason about whether a file upload took effect. User had to implement explicit workaround: queue files and re-inject on every message loop, clearing only when an active container is confirmed.
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss is a high-severity user impact: files are uploaded but silently dropped with zero API feedback. The user's production application lost file uploads without any error indication, requiring significant application-level workarounds (file queuing and re-injection loops). This violates the principle of explicit error handling — the API returns success while silently doing nothing.

source_issues.title: container_upload block silently ignored when no active container exists — undocumented behavior
source_issues.evidence: User reports files sent via container_upload before a container became active were silently dropped with no indication in API response. Had to implement explicit workaround queueing files and re-injecting on every iteration to detect when container becomes active. No error, no warning, no indication in response that upload was ignored.

signals.topic: ServerToolResult not delivered when client tools interrupt stream — orphaned server_tool_use blocks with no matching result
signals.summary: When the Messages API returns stop_reason=tool_use (requesting client tool execution) while server-side tools (code_execution, web_search) are still running in the same turn, the ServerToolResult blocks for those server tools are never delivered — neither during streaming, in the final message, nor in the subsequent API call. This causes orphaned server_tool_use blocks with no result, frontend stuck spinners, and incorrect error detection in monitoring systems.
aliases: server tool result missing after client tool interrupt
server tool result delivery race condition
signals.review_reason: Server tool results being silently dropped in concurrent client+server tool scenarios causes orphaned tool blocks, stuck UI spinners, and incorrect monitoring alerts. The impact is real (observable in production load tests) but the failure mode is specific to a concurrency pattern (server + client tools in same turn). Count is 1 but review_reason provides concrete production evidence from load testing with multiple concurrent users.

source_issues.title: ServerToolResult not delivered when client tools interrupt the stream (code_execution + client tool concurrency)
source_issues.evidence: Production load test with 5 concurrent users shows orphaned text_editor_code_execution and web_search blocks in all concurrent scenarios. Stream ends before server tool results arrive. Server tool result never delivered in any subsequent API call. Frontend stuck spinners and false failure flags in monitoring. Workaround requires emitting synthetic tool_result events.

signals.topic: Streaming tool_use block input arrives double-wrapped in `{ input: {...} }` envelope, breaking schema validation
signals.summary: When using `client.messages.stream()` with forced `tool_choice`, the returned `tool_use` block's `input` field is consistently wrapped one level too deep (`{ input: {...} }` instead of `{...}`). This breaks Zod schema validation, forces users to ship a defensive unwrap workaround, and is 100% reproducible.
signals.review_reason: This is a real bug causing incorrect data structure in every streaming call with forced tool_choice. Users need to write and ship a workaround that runs on every invocation. The issue is marked closed but only after the workaround was described, not fixed. This breaks Zod schema validation in production flows and represents a clear developer experience degradation.

source_issues.title: tool_use block: toolUse.input arrives wrapped in an extra { input: {...} } envelope (streaming, forced tool_choice)
source_issues.evidence: Production diagnostic log shows 100% reproducibility across runs. Users must add defensive unwrap logic inside validation steps. The inner object is well-formed but one level deeper than the SDK type claims. Workaround fires every single run.

signals.topic: Streaming JSON.parse crashes with SyntaxError on invalid escape sequences from model output, crashing the Node process
signals.summary: When Claude outputs strings with regex-like escape sequences (e.g. `\d`, `\p`, `\s`) or other non-strict-JSON content, the streaming parser's JSON.parse throws an unhandled SyntaxError that crashes the entire Node.js process.
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow failure — unhandled SyntaxError crashes the entire Node.js process. Triggered by very common model outputs (regex patterns, Windows paths, LaTeX), meaning users actively hit this in normal workflows. The process crash is a clear, severe user impact with no indication the bug was fixed.

source_issues.title: bug(streaming): JSON.parse crashes on invalid escape sequences in model output
source_issues.evidence: Unhandled SyntaxError crashes the entire Node.js process. The error is unhandled and propagates as an unhandled rejection. Triggered by common model outputs: regex patterns, Windows paths, LaTeX — all common in real usage.

signals.topic: SDK strips directory paths from multipart upload filenames, blocking `skills.versions.create()` with 400 API error
signals.summary: The SDK's multipart form handler calls `getName` with `stripPath=true` by default, converting `my-skill/SKILL.md` to `SKILL.md`. This causes `client.beta.skills.versions.create()` to fail with a 400 API error because the API requires the file to be in a top-level directory structure.
signals.review_reason: This is a key function (`skills.versions.create()`) that is completely blocked — the SDK silently corrupts the upload data so the API rejects it with a 400 error. Users are forced to use a destructive workaround (delete and recreate) rather than version management. Root cause is clearly identified in the SDK code.

source_issues.title: SDK strips directory paths from filenames in multipart uploads, breaking skills.versions.create()
source_issues.evidence: API explicitly returns 400 error: 'SKILL.md file must be exactly in the top-level folder.' The issue shows the exact root cause in `internal/uploads.js` where `stripFilenames` defaults to `true`. Users must delete and recreate skills instead of using `versions.create()` as a workaround.

signals.topic: `betaZodTool` return type `BetaRunnableTool<T>` is not assignable to `ToolUnion`, causing TS2322 error for users following official Ring 5 docs
signals.summary: The official Ring 5 documentation recommends `betaZodTool` for defining typed tools, but its return type `BetaRunnableTool<T>` is incompatible with the `ToolUnion` type required by `messages.stream` and `messages.create`. Users following the docs get a TS2322 error and must use unsafe type casts, defeating the type safety that Zod is supposed to provide.
signals.review_reason: While this doesn't crash or block, it actively misguides users — the official Ring 5 docs recommend betaZodTool but users cannot use it type-safely with messages.stream/create without an unsafe cast. This degrades the developer experience for a prominently documented feature. Count=1 and impact is non-blocking (workaround exists), so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: TS2322: Type BetaRunnableTool<{}> is not assignable to type ToolUnion
source_issues.evidence: Users following the official Ring 5 documentation get a TypeScript TS2322 error. The only workaround is an unsafe cast (`as unknown as Anthropic.Tool`) which removes all type safety. The docs show betaZodTool as the idiomatic approach but provide no type-safe path to use it with messages.stream.

signals.topic: bwrap sandbox does not mount /etc/hosts, breaking localhost DNS resolution in containers
signals.summary: When the SDK's bwrap sandbox is enabled inside a Docker container, /etc/hosts is not bind-mounted into the sandbox namespace, causing localhost DNS resolution to fail. This makes all AWS service calls (via boto3) fail with NameResolutionError when the container routes outbound traffic through a localhost proxy — a standard configuration in AWS Bedrock AgentCore runtimes. Users must disable the sandbox entirely to recover, sacrificing security.
aliases: sandbox DNS resolution failure in containers
localhost proxy DNS resolution broken in sandbox
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（AWS服务调用完全失败），影响生产级容器部署。用户必须禁用sandbox安全机制作为唯一解决方案。复现路径清晰，错误堆栈完整。

source_issues.title: bwrap sandbox does not mount /etc/hosts — breaks localhost DNS resolution in containers
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with full reproduction steps. Error: socket.gaierror [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution when boto3 tries to resolve localhost through a proxy inside a sandboxed container. Workaround is to disable sandbox entirely (sandbox.enabled=false). CLI 2.1.81 had no bwrap sandbox — this regressed in CLI 2.1.92.

signals.topic: Invalid tool_use.id format during session resume causes Anthropic API 400 error
signals.summary: The SDK generates tool_use.id values in the format functions.{ToolName}:{N} (e.g., functions.AskUserQuestion:1), which contain '.' and ':' characters that violate the API's validation pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$. On session resume, these historical messages are replayed verbatim, causing a 400 API error that makes session resume entirely non-functional for sessions with tool calls.
aliases: tool_use.id format validation failure on resume
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（session resume功能完全不可用），有明确API 400错误证据，包含完整无效ID样例。

source_issues.title: Invalid tool_use.id format during session resume causes API 400 error
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with direct API error evidence: 'messages.7.content.1.tool_use.id: String should match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'. Multiple invalid IDs captured (functions.AskUserQuestion:1/2/4/5). Valid IDs from the same session use format 'call_36...' — clear regression in ID generation logic.

signals.topic: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation — users see generic Exception with hard-coded placeholder
signals.summary: When the bundled CLI subprocess exits non-zero, the original ProcessError (with structured exit_code and stderr fields) is destroyed during propagation through the message reader and re-raised as a generic Exception. The stderr field of the original error is itself a hard-coded literal 'Check stderr output for details', never the real subprocess output. Users cannot catch ProcessError, cannot access exit_code, and cannot get actual subprocess stderr, making diagnosing Command failed failures effectively impossible.
signals.review_reason: 关键诊断能力缺失：在CI/并发场景下，ProcessError的exit_code和stderr信息被完全丢弃，用户只能看到硬编码占位符。已有多个相关issue（#515/#282/#238）证明这是反复出现的用户痛点，在并发和CI场景下特别严重。

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with verified reproduction. Actual output shows: caught type=Exception (not ProcessError), has .stderr=False, has .exit_code=False. The error message contains the hardcoded literal 'Check stderr output for details'. Issue explicitly cites #515, #282, #238 as closed issues hitting the same pattern — demonstrates this is a recurring user pain point.

signals.topic: anyio memory object stream resource leak in Query.close()
signals.summary: Query.close() cancels the task group and closes the transport but never calls aclose() on self._message_send or self._message_receive (anyio MemoryObjectSendStream / MemoryObjectReceiveStream pair). These objects are collected by GC with their streams still open, generating ResourceWarning in PYTHONDEVMODE. Long-running processes with many query cycles accumulate unclosed stream handles.
signals.review_reason: 资源泄漏：Query.close()未正确关闭anyio流对象，导致ResourceWarning和句柄积累。在长时间运行的进程（频繁创建query循环）中会引发资源耗尽。提供了完整复现脚本和具体代码行号。

source_issues.title: Resource Leak: anyio memory object stream associated with a query is leaked
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with reproduction script that triggers ResourceWarning: Unclosed <MemoryObjectReceiveStream>. Author notes PR #657 may address it, but issue was filed to boost awareness. Clear code pointers to source of the leak (query.py lines 119-121 and lines 800-814).

signals.topic: get_session_info() returns no AI-generated title for SDK-driven sessions
signals.summary: For sessions driven by the Python SDK, get_session_info() never returns an AI-generated title — it falls back to the first user prompt. The bundled CLI never writes the ai-title line into the session JSONL during SDK-driven sessions, so there is nothing for get_session_info() to surface. The read side (_internal/sessions.py) is correct; the bug is the write side.
aliases: AI session title not persisted in SDK sessions
custom_title returns None for SDK sessions
ai-title not written to session JSONL
signals.review_reason: 关键功能退化：SDK驱动会话的AI生成标题完全不可用，get_session_info()只能返回首条prompt作为fallback。有完整复现代码，且workaround依赖私有API（不稳定）。影响会话管理和导航功能。

source_issues.title: get_session_info() returns no AI-generated title for sessions created via the Python SDK
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with full reproduction code. grep ai-title on the session JSONL returns nothing after long SDK-driven sessions. Author provides a workaround using a private _send_control_request API. This is a regression relative to #161's expected resolution.

signals.topic: beta.sessions stream starvation — 80% of concurrent sessions fail with TypeError before any events arrive
signals.summary: When firing multiple beta.sessions.events.stream() calls (even serially), 4 of 5 consistently fail with 'TypeError: stream error: terminated' before producing any events. The standard Messages API works reliably with the same credentials, making this an isolated regression in the sessions lifecycle that forces users to fall back to a less capable API.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency session failures (80% of attempts) blocking the primary sessions API workflow. Errors occur before any events are produced, meaning the API is completely non-functional for its intended purpose. Users are forced to abandon beta.sessions entirely and fall back to client.messages.create as a workaround.

source_issues.title: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4 of 5 parallel (and serial) sessions fail with TypeError: stream error: terminated before any events
source_issues.evidence: 5 parallel sessions: 1/5 completes. Serial attempts: 4/5 fail with same error. sawAnyEvent=false for all failures. No HTTP error, no APIError. Standard Messages API works fine with same auth. Workaround of using client.messages.create instead works but is not the intended API.

signals.topic: Linux CLI auto-discovery prefers musl binary over glibc — blocks CLI from running on common Linux distros
signals.summary: On Linux systems with both musl and glibc optional dependencies installed (common with pnpm), SDK auto-discovery picks the musl binary first and fails to spawn it with ENOENT. The error message 'Claude Code native binary not found' is misleading since the file exists and is readable, but the musl dynamic loader is missing on glibc systems.
signals.review_reason: Startup crash that blocks the entire CLI from running on the majority of Linux environments (Ubuntu, RHEL, Fedora, Debian all use glibc). pnpm's flat optional dependency model makes this a common occurrence. The only workaround is manually specifying pathToClaudeCodeExecutable, which is a non-obvious friction for SDK users.

source_issues.title: Linux: musl binary preferred over glibc in v0.2.116 CLI auto-discovery
source_issues.evidence: Ubuntu 24.04 (glibc 2.39) with pnpm installs both @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-linux-x64-musl and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-linux-x64. SDK picks musl, spawn fails with ENOENT. Glibc variant works when pathToClaudeCodeExecutable is passed explicitly. Root cause confirmed in sdk.mjs resolver: musl candidate is listed first, try/catch guards require.resolve but not the downstream spawn.

signals.topic: Bundled cli.js undici fails IPv6 happy-eyeballs fallback — Vertex AI OAuth hangs on dual-stack networks with Tailscale
signals.summary: On networks with Tailscale (IPv6 ULA address) where IPv6 is not routable to Google, the bundled undici HTTP client fails to fall back to IPv4. This causes OAuth token refresh to hang and all chat messages to fail with empty error, while sessions list and calendar continue working.
signals.review_reason: Auth-blocking issue that makes the entire SDK unusable on Tailscale (a very common VPN/tool). All chat messages fail with empty OAuth error while other features continue working, making the failure silent and hard to diagnose. The root cause is in the bundled CLI's undici HTTP client configuration, not user-configurable.

source_issues.title: Bundled cli.js fails IPv6 happy-eyeballs fallback — Vertex AI OAuth hangs on dual-stack networks
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed on Tailscale networks with IPv6 ULA (fd7a::). Node native https module handles the fallback correctly (returns 400 OK). Undici's autoSelectFamily fails to fall back to IPv4. Workarounds: local DNS resolver stripping AAAA records, NODE_OPTIONS preload patching dns.lookup. Repro script in issue body.

signals.topic: query() with outputFormat json_schema crashes with internal null dereference (effortLevel)
signals.summary: A minimal query() call using only outputFormat with json_schema crashes deterministically with an internal SDK TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel'). The failure is a null dereference inside the bundled CLI before any structured output is returned, surfacing as a result error. Affects SDK v0.1.75 and earlier across multiple releases.
signals.review_reason: Internal SDK crash that makes structured output entirely unusable for users relying on outputFormat. The error is a null dereference in internal SDK code, not a validation or configuration error, meaning it cannot be handled gracefully by SDK consumers. A 25-line repro exists with deterministic reproduction.

source_issues.title: query() with minimal outputFormat: { type: "json_schema" } can crash internally with Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel')
source_issues.evidence: 25-line repro with only outputFormat.json_schema with empty schema. Crashes deterministically. Surface error: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading effortLevel)' in bundled cli.js. Longstanding bug across multiple SDK versions (oldest tested also affected). Internal null dereference in effort-resolution path, not a user-facing contract error.

signals.topic: outputFormat json_schema returns subtype 'success' but structured_output is undefined for complex schemas — silent failure
signals.summary: When using outputFormat with non-trivial json_schema (nested objects, arrays, enums, $ref), the SDK returns result with subtype 'success' but structured_output is absent/undefined. The model produces correct JSON in the text result, but the SDK does not extract or validate it. The result type misleadingly indicates success while the intended structured output is missing.
signals.review_reason: Silent failure that breaks structured output for common real-world schemas with nested objects, arrays, and enums. The SDK returns 'success' subtype while the intended structured_output field is missing, misleading SDK consumers into believing the operation succeeded when their parsing code will receive undefined. This is a different root cause from the crash in #299.

source_issues.title: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' when structured_output is absent — should return error_max_structured_output_retries
source_issues.evidence: Simple 2-field schemas work (structured_output populated). Nested schemas (3+ levels) return subtype 'success' with structured_output undefined. Raw Messages API handles these schemas correctly, proving it's an SDK-specific extraction failure. Table of 4 tested schema variants in issue body shows all complex ones fail.

cache save retry on same ref

source_issues.evidence: Agent mode silently discards the session summary output—the SDK generates a complete review but it never reaches GitHub because cleanup skips updateCommentLink when commentId is undefined.

source_issues.evidence: On pull_request events, bundled MCP servers (github_comment, github_inline_comment) never spawn despite correct config build, leaving mcp_servers empty and causing Claude to fail tool calls with 'No such tool available'.

source_issues.title: Usage spikes drastically after /compact command and even after running claude --version
source_issues.evidence: Max 5x ($100/month) subscriber. /compact with a small prompt caused 34% usage jump. 'claude --version' (local, no API call) caused 64% → 100% jump. No warning before /compact. Support confirmed no refund recourse. Wider pattern reported by multiple Max plan subscribers.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Claude Max weekly usage limit window shorter than 7 days
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #53018. Weekly window resets Tuesday 12:00 on Friday April 24 — only 4 days, not 7. Window has shrunk twice on this account. Direct billing/quota impact.

signals.review_reason: Explicit cost impact: user lost 2 of 3 free-trial slots for zero output. The core feature is broken for trial users — they cannot evaluate the product. The task is misreported as 'completed' when it actually failed, masking the error and preventing user retry.

source_issues.title: /ultrareview returns empty findings after rate limit error — burns free trial slots
source_issues.evidence: User lost 2 of 3 free trial slots on a 22k-line diff. Session IDs provided (session_01FwYeGQ15mhZrthPqycLVdf, session_01LugWVBs5zwqdTvDsLK29qt). Explicit server-side rate limit message observed. Findings returned as [] and task marked 'completed' with no error shown to user.

signals.topic: Stream idle timeout blocks main workflow on high-usage paid plan

signals.review_reason: Primary workflow is completely blocked for a high-paying subscriber. Hours of troubleshooting (reset, restart) did not resolve. Regression from a previously working version. No workaround available.

source_issues.evidence: Max subscriber ($200/month) on Opus 4.6. Error: 'API Error: Stream idle timeout - partial response received'. Tried reset and restart multiple times for hours. Regression from v4.6. Screenshot attached showing error UI.

signals.topic: Worktree creation hangs indefinitely on macOS — git stdin socket never written to
signals.summary: Claude.app on macOS hangs forever when creating a worktree. A spawned 'git merge --ff-only' process is blocked reading from a Unix socket that Claude.app opened but never wrote to or closed. The UI is stuck permanently and subsequent worktree attempts queue behind the first.
signals.review_reason: Core workflow (worktree creation) is permanently blocked on macOS. The hang is reliable and worsens with repo size. Full diagnostic evidence (stack trace, lsof) confirms the root cause: stdin attached to a socket that is never written to. No recovery without manual process kill.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Worktree creation hangs indefinitely: spawned 'git merge --ff-only' blocked reading stdin (unix socket never written to / closed)
source_issues.evidence: Full diagnostic evidence provided: process stack trace (read_in_full blocked in read()), lsof output showing stdin as Unix socket with no writer. 40+ existing worktrees in repo. Workaround requires killing the process manually. Related issues #42752, #32091, #53011 cited.

signals.topic: /rewind hangs CLI with no recovery — Ctrl+C ineffective
signals.summary: The /rewind slash command hangs the CLI immediately after checkpoint selection regardless of session size. Ctrl+C cannot interrupt the hang; kill -9 is required. Makes session history navigation completely unavailable.
signals.review_reason: Core session navigation is permanently blocked with no interrupt possible. Users cannot review earlier context, retry prior steps, or escape via /rewind-to-message. The workaround (kill -9 + new session) means losing all session state.

source_issues.title: /rewind hangs the CLI on any session; Ctrl+C does not interrupt
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces on multiple sessions including small fresh sessions. 0–1% CPU matches a synchronous blocking call. Ctrl+C has no effect. Only kill -9 recovers. Distinct from #52995 (large-session resume) — /rewind hangs on any session size. 2 comments, related to #52995.

signals.topic: Skills introduction notebook missing GitHub repo prerequisite step
signals.summary: The skills-notebooks-01-skills-introduction notebook instructs users to 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' without mentioning that the GitHub repo must be cloned first. Users land on the page to learn about skills but cannot follow the first step, causing confusion and frustration.
aliases: missing prerequisites in skills intro notebook

source_issues.title: [BUG] intro to skills should point at github repo as install prereq
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports being unable to follow instructions without first cloning a GitHub repo that is never mentioned. States 'be frustrated' as end state of reproduction steps. Filed as bug by end user.

signals.topic: ralph-loop: --stdin handler word-splits multi-word flag values — completion promise silently corrupted to first word only
signals.summary: The ralph-loop setup-ralph-loop.sh uses 'set -- \$var' (unquoted) for --stdin argument parsing. This causes shell word-splitting on whitespace, destroying multi-word --completion-promise values. A promise like 'there were not any improvement or repair findings' becomes just "'there" — and the stop hook then matches prematurely on that fragment. The corruption is silent with no error, making it hard to debug why the loop exits unexpectedly.
signals.review_reason: Two related ralph-loop state corruption issues: (1) multi-word flag values are silently destroyed causing premature loop exits, (2) concurrent loops in the same directory overwrite each other's state files. Both corrupt the loop's core state logic without any error signal. Issue 1562 is a single-user bug; issue 1542 is a multi-session bug — both affect the fundamental loop contract.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: --stdin handler word-splits multi-word flag values (silent corruption of --completion-promise)
source_issues.evidence: User runs /ralph-loop do some work --completion-promise 'there were not any improvement or repair findings'. After setup, .claude/ralph-loop.local.md contains: completion_promise: "'there" — the full sentence is silently truncated to the first word. The stop hook then matches on <promise>'there</promise>, which Claude can accidentally emit immediately, causing premature loop exit.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: Cannot run multiple concurrent loops in the same project directory
source_issues.evidence: State file path is hardcoded to .claude/ralph-loop.local.md. Two concurrent /ralph-loop sessions in the same project directory overwrite each other's state. Session 1's loop then runs session 2's prompt or exits due to session_id mismatch. Root cause: fixed filename with no per-session namespacing in stop-hook.sh line 13.

signals.topic: remember plugin: SessionStart/PostToolUse hooks fail on first run — startup hook error blocks plugin use
signals.summary: The remember plugin's hooks.json redirects stderr to .remember/logs/hook-errors.log, but the logs directory is created only AFTER the shell tries to open the redirect target. On every fresh project, new git worktree, or first-ever invocation, the shell fails with 'No such file or directory' and emits 'SessionStart:startup hook error'. This is a reliable, reproducible first-run blocker.
aliases: SessionStart hook error on fresh project
signals.review_reason: Reliably reproducible first-run blocker. Every new project/worktree/first-invocation user hits this error, preventing the remember plugin from functioning at all. The hook harness reports 'startup hook error' which is a clear user-facing block.

source_issues.title: remember: SessionStart/PostToolUse hooks fail with "No such file or directory" when .remember/logs/ is absent
source_issues.evidence: Shell redirect to .remember/logs/hook-errors.log fails because the directory does not yet exist. Reproduces on fresh projects, git worktrees, and first-ever invocation. Error: '/bin/sh: <project>/.remember/logs/hook-errors.log: No such file or directory' followed by 'SessionStart:startup hook error'.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: orphaned server.ts processes spin at 100% CPU — SIGTERM fallback to SIGKILL missing
signals.summary: When a previous Telegram plugin server.ts becomes an orphan (parent crash, hard kill, OS sleep), the stale-poller sends SIGTERM only. If the orphan is in a retry loop, it ignores SIGTERM. The PID file is then overwritten with the new PID, leaving two or more pollers competing at ~100% CPU indefinitely. Users experience laptop overheating and fans spinning up with no resolution.
signals.review_reason: Orphaned processes at 100% CPU is a clear resource-exhaustion issue that causes observable harm (laptop overheating, fan noise). The fix is simple (add SIGKILL fallback after SIGTERM), but absent it the problem persists indefinitely until manually killed.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: stale server.ts can spin at 100% CPU — SIGTERM fallback missing
source_issues.evidence: Stale-poller at server.ts:60-68 sends SIGTERM only. Processes in 409-Conflict retry loops ignore SIGTERM. PID file is overwritten, leaving multiple pollers at 99-100% CPU. Symptom: bun server.ts processes stuck at 99-100% CPU for hours, laptop runs hot, fans spin up.

signals.topic: explanatory-output-style plugin: hangs new sessions at prompt-submit on macOS — Claude Code unusable after plugin load
signals.summary: On macOS, enabling explanatory-output-style v1.0.0 causes new Claude Code sessions to hang at prompt-submit time. The session banner renders and keystrokes work, but pressing Enter does nothing — UserPromptSubmit never fires. Pre-existing sessions are unaffected. Disabling the plugin restores new sessions. This effectively blocks Claude Code usage after plugin installation.
signals.review_reason: Plugin causes new sessions to become unusable — UserPromptSubmit never fires, Enter has no effect. This is a functional block of the primary workflow (writing and submitting prompts). The user must disable the plugin to recover, defeating the purpose of having it installed.

source_issues.title: [macOS] explanatory-output-style hangs new sessions at prompt-submit (no exec-perm/Windows path bug)
source_issues.evidence: After enabling explanatory-output-style@claude-plugins-official v1.0.0, new sessions hang at prompt-submit. Enter does nothing, UserPromptSubmit never fires. Pre-existing sessions unaffected. Disabling plugin restores new sessions. Script has correct perms (755) and LF line endings. Not a Windows path issue, not an exec permission issue — fresh macOS-specific hang.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: inbound channel notifications not received by Claude Code — MCP server generates correct JSON-RPC but messages don't appear
signals.summary: Telegram plugin 0.0.6 successfully sends outbound messages and the MCP server is connected, but inbound messages from Telegram users never appear in the Claude Code session. The server.ts manually generates correct JSON-RPC notifications (verified on stdout), but Claude Code 2.1.117 does not display them. The core channel integration is completely non-functional for receiving messages.
signals.review_reason: The primary function of a messaging channel plugin — receiving inbound messages — is completely broken. The MCP server correctly generates notifications but Claude Code never displays them. Users cannot receive messages via the Telegram channel despite a fully connected and functional MCP server.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin 0.0.6: inbound notifications not received by Claude Code
source_issues.evidence: Outbound works (reply tool sends messages). MCP server shows connected. Running server.ts manually shows valid JSON-RPC notifications on stdout: {"method":"notifications/claude/channel",...}. Claude Code 2.1.117 does not display messages. No errors in /plugin Errors tab. Both pairing and allowlist DM policies fail identically. Core receive functionality is completely broken.

signals.topic: Tutorial references retired/deprecated Claude Haiku 3 model causing learning flow blockage
signals.summary: The interactive tutorial still references Claude Haiku 3 which has been recently retired, causing users following the exercises to hit a non-functional model and be unable to complete tutorial steps.
signals.review_reason: 用户反映教程引用的 Claude Haiku 3 模型已被下架（recently-retired），导致跟随教程练习的用户在调用该模型时会遭遇主流程失败。虽为单 issue，但模型不可用属于关键功能不可用，且教程类项目的内容错误直接影响学习路径，归类为 P1。

source_issues.title: Tutorial using Haiku 3- needs update
source_issues.evidence: User reports the tutorial still uses recently-retired Claude Haiku 3 and needs updating to 4.5. The retired model means users trying to run the tutorial exercises will encounter a non-functional model, blocking the core learning flow.

signals.topic: Command injection vulnerability in with_server.py due to subprocess shell=True on unvalidated user input
signals.summary: The with_server.py script uses subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True) with a CLI-supplied --server argument. When invoked by an AI agent from a prompt-driven workflow, a malicious or injected --server value can execute arbitrary shell commands on the host, creating a command injection attack surface in agentic usage contexts.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine security vulnerability with a working PoC, not a generic security keyword match. The with_server.py script is a real tool invoked by Claude-driven workflows where untrusted input (from READMEs, issue bodies, or tool outputs) can reach the --server argument. shell=True on unsanitized CLI input enables arbitrary shell command execution on the host, which is a critical security issue that can lead to host compromise in agentic usage contexts. The attack surface is real: even 'trusted CLI input' collapses when an agent copies args from documentation.

source_issues.title: with_server.py: command injection via --server in Popen shell=True
source_issues.evidence: POC demonstrates arbitrary shell command execution via --server argument: python with_server.py --server "python -m http.server; touch /tmp/pwned". The script uses shell=True with unsanitized CLI input, enabling command injection when used in AI agent workflows where agents copy-paste arguments from READMEs, issue bodies, or tool outputs.

signals.topic: pack.py bundles .DS_Store on macOS causing Microsoft Office to flag output files as corrupt or requiring repair
signals.summary: scripts/office/pack.py does not filter .DS_Store files created by macOS Finder. When repacking PPTX/DOCX/XLSX files, the bundled .DS_Store causes Microsoft Office (365) to display a 'found a problem with content' repair dialog or fail to open entirely. The issue affects all three office skills (pptx, docx, xlsx) that share the same pack.py script.
aliases: macOS DS_Store corruption of Office files
pack.py includes .DS_Store causing Office repair dialog
Office files corrupt after pack.py on macOS
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow failure, not a theoretical concern. Verified reproduction on Microsoft 365 for Mac demonstrates that the pack.py output is broken for Office users on macOS — files either show a repair dialog or fail to open entirely. The issue is reproducible in both directions and affects all three office skills sharing the same script. While the issue is macOS-specific and lower frequency, the impact is significant: Office users cannot use the output of the skill.

source_issues.title: pack.py bundles .DS_Store on macOS, causing Office to flag files as corrupt
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on Microsoft 365 for Mac: unpack PPTX with unpack.py, open folder in Finder (creates .DS_Store), repack with pack.py, open in PowerPoint → repair dialog. Deleting .DS_Store before repacking produces a clean file. ECMA-376 spec requires all archive entries to be declared in [Content_Types].xml; Office rejects undeclared entries. Affects pptx/docx/xlsx skills sharing the same pack.py script (SHA db29ed8b).

signals.topic: Skills lack environment setup documentation causing ModuleNotFoundError when users run Python scripts
signals.summary: Multiple skills contain Python scripts with third-party dependencies (pandas, requests, opencv, etc.) but do not document how to set up the required virtual environment. This causes ModuleNotFoundError at runtime, requiring users to manually figure out which packages to install, creating a poor onboarding experience.
aliases: no dependency installation instructions in skills
signals.review_reason: While this is documented as a feature request/enhancement rather than a crash, the issue explicitly describes a real user pain: ModuleNotFoundError at runtime across multiple skills when users try to run scripts. The problem is that skills don't provide venv setup or dependency installation instructions, so users hit import errors and must reverse-engineer what's needed. The pdf skill is cited as a model that already handles this correctly, demonstrating the gap. This is a recurring onboarding failure across many skills, not a one-off. Confidence is slightly reduced because there is no external corroboration from multiple users yet.

source_issues.title: [bug] Add Environment setup to skills
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly describes ModuleNotFoundError when users try to run Python scripts across skills that use third-party packages (pandas, requests, numpy, opencv, beautifulsoup4, openpyxl, python-docx). The issue cites the pdf skill as a positive example that already has proper environment setup documentation, and proposes a standardized template. Explicitly describes poor user experience for newcomers and time wasted on import errors.

signals.topic: mcp-builder skill contains stale API references and bugs in documentation causing copy-paste failures
signals.summary: The mcp-builder skill documentation contains multiple outdated or incorrect API examples: deprecated Pydantic v2 field attributes, wrong ctx.elicit() signature, incorrect lifespan pattern attribute names, missing Node.js imports, wrong registerResource() signatures, and use of deprecated notification APIs. These cause copy-paste failures when developers follow the documentation to build MCP servers.
aliases: stale FastMCP API examples in docs
mcp-builder copy-paste failures from documentation errors
signals.review_reason: This is not a generic 'documentation needs improvement' issue — it documents actual code correctness problems in the mcp-builder skill that cause runtime failures or compile errors when users follow the docs. Key failures include: Pydantic emits PydanticDeprecatedSince20 warnings, ctx.elicit() signature mismatch will throw TypeError at runtime, lifespan context attribute name mismatch will cause KeyError, and missing Node imports cause immediate compile failure. The mcp-builder skill is a reference implementation for building MCP servers; incorrect docs mean developers building production MCP servers will encounter failures. These are developer experience failures with direct functional impact.

source_issues.title: Bugs and stale API references in the mcp-builder skill
source_issues.evidence: 11 distinct documentation bugs catalogued: (1) max_items deprecated in Pydantic v2, (2) ctx.elicit() signature wrong — uses prompt/input_type that don't exist, (3) lifespan pattern wrong — wrong attribute names (lifespan_state vs lifespan_context), (4) missing imports in Node complete example causing compile failure, (5) registerResource signature wrong and registerResourceList doesn't exist, (6) deprecated notification API used instead of typed helpers, (7) server naming inconsistency, (8) destructiveHint semantics confusion, (9) misleading 'Avoid SSE' guidance, (10) opinionated response_format recommendation. Author has a working patched copy and offers to submit a PR.

signals.topic: docx skill TableOfContents renders empty in Google Docs due to missing cachedEntries option
signals.summary: The docx skill's TableOfContents example creates .docx files that render correctly in Microsoft Word, but when uploaded to Google Drive and converted to Google Docs, the TOC renders as an empty placeholder with non-resolving hyperlinks. This is because docx-js only emits a populated TOC cache when cachedEntries is provided, and Google Docs relies on the cached content rather than running field updates on open.
aliases: TOC placeholder in Google Docs conversion
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine cross-platform rendering bug, not a theoretical concern. The TOC works in Microsoft Word but renders empty in Google Docs due to a missing cachedEntries option. For users who generate .docx files and share them for Google Docs collaboration (a common workflow), the TOC is broken. The root cause is clearly identified (docx-js cache behavior) and the fix is well-defined. Impact is real but limited to Google Docs integration use case, making it P2 rather than P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug] docx skill: TableOfContents renders empty in Google Docs without cachedEntries
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: docx-js only emits populated <w:sdt> cache when cachedEntries is provided. Google Docs does not run TOC field update on open and relies on cached content. The bug manifests as empty TOC placeholders in Google Docs with non-resolving hyperlinks after clicking refresh. Verified working in Microsoft Word (TOC renders correctly), broken in Google Docs conversion. Fix: document cachedEntries option in SKILL.md and flag in Critical Rules.

signals.topic: Context limit from provider API is discarded, causing local/custom models to default to wrong 128k limit
signals.summary: Goose discards the context limit returned by LiteLLM/OpenAI-compatible provider APIs, silently falling back to 128k for local .gguf models and custom providers with uppercase names. This causes model overflow crashes, broken auto-compaction, and wrong context usage reporting.
aliases: provider context limit not exposed in Desktop UI
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues all root-caused to context limit mishandling in Goose. Issue #8835 causes actual crashes when local models are overflowed with >128k tokens. Issue #8780 blocks users from configuring context for custom providers via the UI. Issue #8752 silently misconfigures any uppercase-named custom model. All three are independently reproducible with clear user-facing failure modes (model crash, wrong context usage %, inability to configure).

source_issues.title: Context limit from Provider API is discarded, causing fallback to 128k for local models
source_issues.evidence: Goose discards max_input_tokens from provider API and defaults to 128k. Local models with 8k context (e.g. Qwen) overflow and crash during long sessions.

source_issues.title: Custom provider context_limit not reflected in Desktop UI — hard to change from 128K default
source_issues.evidence: Settings UI shows no context_limit field. Custom Headers field is misleading — sending context_limit as HTTP header has no effect on Goose's internal context management.

source_issues.title: Case mismatch in custom provider model name breaks context_limit lookup
source_issues.evidence: Model names saved with original case (e.g. GLM-5.1) but compared case-sensitively against lowercase GOOSE_MODEL, causing silent 128k fallback for any model with uppercase letters.

signals.topic: Goose CLI immediately backgrounds itself on startup (SIGTSTP), requiring manual fg
signals.summary: On certain terminal emulators (Tilix, Fedora Linux), Goose CLI immediately stops itself (SIGTSTP) right after initialization, showing 'Stopped' in the shell job list before the prompt ever becomes interactive.
signals.review_reason: Two reports from different Linux distributions (Arch/Tilix, Fedora) confirm the same behavior — Goose CLI immediately backgrounds itself on startup, making the session non-interactive without manual intervention. This is a complete workflow blocker for affected terminal environments. The workaround (TERM=xterm) is non-obvious and not documented.

source_issues.title: Goose session immediately stops (backgrounded) on startup in Tilix terminal
source_issues.evidence: Tilix on Arch Linux: process immediately suspends (SIGTSTP) right after 'goose is ready'. Shell shows '[4]+ Stopped goose session'. User must manually run fg to resume.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Goose CLI backgrounds on launch (version 1.32.0 on Linux)
source_issues.evidence: Fedora Linux: 'goose' command immediately moves to background. Shell shows 'Stopped goose'. User must manually fg to interact. Reproduced on clean install of v1.32.0.

signals.topic: DeepSeek V4 thinking/reasoning mode causes 400 error on multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: Goose strips thinking/reasoning content from assistant responses when building message history, causing DeepSeek V4 API to return 400 errors on the second turn of any multi-turn conversation, making sustained sessions impossible.
aliases: multi-turn conversation fails with reasoning mode
signals.review_reason: Deterministic workflow breakage for DeepSeek V4 reasoning/thinking mode users. Multi-turn conversations fail consistently on the second turn with explicit API 400 errors. While only one report, the failure is deterministic and blocks the core use case of maintaining a conversation context. No workaround except starting a new session for every exchange, which defeats the purpose of multi-turn interaction.

source_issues.title: deepseek-v4 thinking mode error
source_issues.evidence: Multi-turn conversations fail with explicit 400 error: 'The content[].thinking in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.' (native) or 'reasoning_content must be passed back' (OpenAI-compatible). First turn works; all subsequent turns fail deterministically.

signals.topic: Goose Desktop app gets stuck on white screen and crashes on startup
signals.summary: On Windows, after an unexpected shutdown with an active Goose session, the Desktop app fails to start — getting stuck on a white screen indefinitely before crashing, with no way to recover except waiting or reinstalling.
signals.review_reason: App completely fails to start on Windows after an unclean shutdown scenario, presenting a white screen then crashing. This renders the Desktop app entirely unusable for affected users, with no diagnostic path accessible (user cannot reach goose-docs.ai). Affects two different versions (1.17 and 1.32) suggesting a persistent issue. Confidence reduced slightly because the root cause (pricing cache + LM Studio state) is not fully diagnosed and only one report.

source_issues.title: Getting stuck at white screen and then crashing
source_issues.evidence: Windows 10: After unclean shutdown with LM Studio connected, Goose Desktop (v1.17 and v1.32) shows white screen for several seconds then crashes. No interaction possible. Affects both old and latest versions. Logs show pricing cache init failure followed by agent server startup.

signals.topic: ACP provider streaming responses render as separate Desktop message bubbles instead of a single coalesced message
signals.summary: Streaming text from ACP providers (claude-acp, amp-acp, codex-acp, copilot-acp, pi-acp) renders as dozens of discrete timestamped bubbles in the Desktop UI instead of accumulating into one streaming message, making the conversation view unusable.
aliases: streaming not coalescing in desktop UI
separate text chunks render as individual messages
signals.review_reason: Desktop UI is functionally broken for all ACP provider users — streaming responses are fragmented into dozens of separate message bubbles, making the conversation view unreadable. Root cause is clearly identified in the Rust backend (missing message ID per stream session). The CLI is unaffected, confirming this is a real rendering defect, not an API issue.

source_issues.title: ACP providers: streaming text chunks render as separate Desktop message bubbles
source_issues.evidence: ACP streaming produces ~20+ separate message bubbles, each with its own timestamp and containing only a few tokens or a sentence fragment. The same prompt via CLI produces a single clean response. Root cause identified: ACP backend yields Message with id:None per chunk, so useChatStream.ts coalescing check never matches.

signals.topic: Screenshot MIME type hardcoded to PNG in CUA clients causes data corruption with JPEG images
signals.summary: GoogleCUAClient and AnthropicCUAClient hardcode mimeType/media_type as 'image/png' and only strip PNG data URL prefixes. When screenshots are JPEG, the base64 payload retains the wrong prefix and mismatched MIME metadata is sent, leading to malformed tool responses.
aliases: hardcoded PNG mimeType in CUA image handling
JPEG screenshot data URL prefix not stripped in CUA clients
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues (#2046, #2035) independently report the same root cause: CUA clients hardcode PNG mimeType and only strip PNG data URL prefixes. When JPEG screenshots are used, this causes malformed base64 payloads and mismatched MIME metadata in tool responses. This corrupts the image data passed to the AI model, directly impacting the reliability of screenshot-based agent tasks.

source_issues.title: core(cua): Google function-response image handling hardcodes PNG mimeType
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states mismatched metadata is sent when screenshot input is JPEG, and the full data URL may be passed instead of raw base64 payload, corrupting tool responses.

source_issues.title: core(cua): Anthropic tool_result image handling hardcodes PNG media type
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states JPEG input results in incorrect metadata and malformed base64 payload because non-PNG prefix is not removed.

signals.topic: Non-OpenAI CUA clients silently drop runtime context notes, causing repeated captcha interactions and unreliable task continuation
signals.summary: V3CuaAgentHandler injects captcha guidance via addContextNote(), but only OpenAICUAClient consumes these notes. GoogleCUAClient, AnthropicCUAClient, and MicrosoftCUAClient all silently drop them, leading to repeated captcha clicks and failed task flows.
aliases: addContextNote not implemented in non-OpenAI CUA providers
captcha context notes dropped by Google/Anthropic/Microsoft CUA clients
signals.review_reason: Issue #2037 documents a concrete behavioral gap: V3CuaAgentHandler relies on addContextNote() to inject captcha state guidance, but Google, Anthropic, and Microsoft CUA clients all silently no-op this method. The result is repeated captcha interactions (the agent clicks an already-solved captcha again) and unreliable task continuation — a direct workflow failure for non-OpenAI users.

source_issues.title: core(cua): implement addContextNote parity for Google/Anthropic/Microsoft clients
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states non-OpenAI CUA providers silently drop important runtime guidance (e.g. 'captcha already solved; do not click again'), causing repeated captcha interaction and less reliable task continuation. Documented behavior across 3 provider clients.

signals.topic: Anthropic CUA client ignores maxImages option, making screenshot retention tuning ineffective
signals.summary: ClientOptions.maxImages existed as a user-configurable option, but AnthropicCUAClient always used default compression behavior (keep 2), ignoring the user's setting. Users who tune maxImages for Microsoft CUA get no effect with Anthropic.
aliases: Anthropic CUA ignores maxImages client option
screenshot compression maxImages not wired for Anthropic CUA
signals.review_reason: maxImages is an existing user-facing option for tuning screenshot retention. Anthropic CUA silently ignores this option and always defaults to keeping 2 screenshots. This is a config drift bug: the option works for Microsoft CUA but is non-functional for Anthropic, leading to wasted context tokens and higher cost for users who expect the option to work.

source_issues.title: fix(core): honor maxImages in Anthropic CUA screenshot compression
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states maxImages option existed but Anthropic CUA always used default compression behavior, meaning users who set this option for other providers see no effect with Anthropic — the option is effectively broken for this provider.

signals.topic: waitForFirstTopLevelPage timeout of 5000ms is not configurable, blocking low-performance environments
signals.summary: The browser initialization timeout is hardcoded to 5000ms. Users on low-performance hardware report TimeoutError during Stagehand initialization, with no way to increase the timeout.
aliases: waitForFirstTopLevelPage timeout too short for slow machines
signals.review_reason: The init() method fails with a hardcoded 5000ms timeout that cannot be overridden. A user on low-performance hardware is completely blocked from using Stagehand, with no configuration option to increase the timeout. This is a main-flow blockage (init is the first step of every Stagehand workflow). Only a workaround comment was provided, not a proper fix.

source_issues.title: TimeoutError: waitForFirstTopLevelPage (no top-level Page) timed out after 5000ms
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports the timeout error on a low-performance computer and asks if the timeout can be increased. The issue was closed with no evidence of the timeout being made configurable, only a workaround comment suggesting 'headless: false' as a temporary fix.

signals.topic: LoopDetectionMiddleware误判合法科学计算工作流为主流程阻断
signals.summary: LoopDetectionMiddleware的per-tool frequency硬限制（默认50次bash调用）将合法的科学计算批处理工作流（如RNA-seq多样本分析）错误识别为无限循环，直接导致400错误和对话不可恢复，用户已完成的工作流被强制中断。
aliases: bash tool frequency hard limit interrupts scientific workflows
signals.review_reason: 该问题在2条issue中有明确用户影响证据：(1)科学工作流被强制中断，LLM返回400错误不可恢复；(2)LoopDetectionMiddleware设计缺陷（硬编码per-tool频率而非progress-aware）已形成系统性反复误判，RFC#2517明确指出该问题会成为主流程阻断器。count虽为2，但review_reason给出强证据表明workflow-blocking+P0合理。

source_issues.title: Loop Detection Middleware Incorrectly Interrupts Scientific Workflows with Repeated Tool Calls
source_issues.evidence: RNA-seq differential expression analysis工作流在处理15+样本时，middleware强制注入[LOOP DETECTED]消息，导致LLM请求返回400错误 InvalidParameter，provider拒绝该消息结构体，对话无法恢复。提供了完整堆栈日志和截图。

source_issues.title: Loop Detection Limit Too Restrictive for Scientific Computing Workflows
source_issues.evidence: LoopDetectionMiddleware的_DEFAULT_TOOL_FREQ_HARD_LIMIT=50导致生物信息学工作流（15样本RNA-seq分析）在第53次bash调用时被强制停止，用户被迫用subagent作为workaround，影响主流程连续性。提供了复现步骤。

signals.topic: write_file工具生成文件内容被截断导致HTML显示乱码
signals.summary: 用户使用write_file工具生成HTML文件时，内容总是被截断（丢失头部或尾部代码），导致生成的HTML页面显示乱码，无法完成预期内容生成任务。
signals.review_reason: 用户通过截图明确展示了write_file生成HTML文件被截断导致乱码的完整问题现场，虽仅1条issue但有截图证据，属于主流程失败（内容生成不完整）。P0需要count>=3，当前count=1降为P1。

source_issues.title: 写文件是否有长度限制，生成的HTML总会被截断
source_issues.evidence: 用户通过截图展示了生成HTML被截断（头部丢失或尾部丢失）导致显示乱码的问题，用户明确询问write_file工具是否存在长度限制。提供了两张截图作为证据。

signals.topic: extractContentFromMessage使用换行拼接content array导致Markdown碎片化和React hydration错误

aliases: 细粒度delta模型消息碎片化

source_issues.title: extractContentFromMessage用\n拼接content array导致碎片化

、导出文件每个token一行。提供了具体代码位置(frontend/src/core/messages/utils.ts:192)和完整复现步骤。

signals.topic: LocalSandboxProvider自定义挂载符号链接逃逸沙箱边界读取/写入受限范围外文件

aliases: custom mount symlink sandbox boundary bypass
signals.review_reason: 沙箱安全边界逃逸是严重安全问题，可导致agent读取/写入受限范围外的主机路径。RFC#2506有P1标签且提供了完整复现步骤，虽仅1条issue但安全问题本身具有高严重性，P1合理。

source_issues.title: [P1] Local custom mount symlinks can escape sandbox boundary
source_issues.evidence: RFC文档明确指出LocalSandboxProvider在处理自定义挂载时只验证虚拟路径前缀，解析后的真实路径未重新验证挂载根目录，符号链接可指向外部。只读挂载可通过符号链接被写入。提供了具体受影响文件路径和复现步骤。

source_issues.title: Abnormal configuration of MIMO large model

source_issues.title: mimo 大模型 配置异常

signals.topic: Resume task button incorrectly shown for completed tasks when hooks are enabled on Windows

hooks state not cleared on task completion

signals.topic: Windows cmd Chinese output garbled despite chcp 65001 UTF-8 code page

signals.topic: Context window percentage display caps at wrong maximum (32.8k instead of configured value)

source_issues.title: Context window percentage display incorrectly caps at 32.8k

signals.topic: API errors causing workflow blockage — 402/429/401/connection errors across multiple providers
signals.summary: Users encounter various API errors preventing Continue from functioning: 402 (no credits on Continue proxy), 429 (Gemini quota exceeded), 401 (invalid Anthropic API key), LMaaS connection errors, and GPT-5 Mini returning HTML instead of JSON. All block the primary workflow with no fallback.
aliases: provider API failures preventing Continue from working
signals.review_reason: Five distinct issues across multiple providers (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI/LMaaS) all block the primary Continue workflow with no graceful fallback. Count=5 meets the P0 threshold. Each error type (402 credit exhaustion, 429 quota, 401 auth, connection error, malformed response) represents a real user blockage where the AI-assisted coding workflow cannot proceed at all.

source_issues.title: Error: Claude Sonnet 4.6 - 402
source_issues.evidence: Continue proxy returns 402 'You have no credits remaining' for Claude Sonnet 4.6 — primary workflow completely blocked.

source_issues.title: Error: Gemini 3 Pro - Unknown error

source_issues.title: Error: LMaaS - Codestral - Unknown error

source_issues.title: concuniu
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 401 Unauthorized from Anthropic API with 'invalid x-api-key'; primary workflow blocked.

source_issues.title: Error: GPT-5 Mini - Unknown error
source_issues.evidence: API returns HTML '<!DOCTYPE' instead of JSON; JSON parse fails with 'Unexpected token'; primary workflow blocked.

signals.topic: CLI silent installation failure — exits with exit code 127 and no actionable error message
signals.summary: The CLI install script fails silently with only 'Installation failed. Cleaning up...' and exit code 127, with no indication that npm is missing due to a partial Node.js installation. This completely blocks new users from installing the CLI, providing zero actionable information to diagnose the root cause.
aliases: CLI install fails with no error message
signals.review_reason: Clear startup-blocking bug: new users cannot install the CLI at all. The failure is silent with zero actionable diagnostics, which directly prevents onboarding. Evidence includes full install log showing exit code 127 with 'npm config get prefix' being the last command before cleanup.

source_issues.title: CLI install can fail with no error message
source_issues.evidence: Install script exits with exit code 127 and 'Installation failed. Cleaning up...' with no explanation; root cause is npm binary missing due to partial Node.js installation. No diagnostic message shown to user.

signals.topic: Autocomplete broken for OpenAI-compatible self-hosted endpoints — sends wrong request format to /completions
signals.summary: When using OpenAI-compatible self-hosted models with the 'autocomplete' role, Continue sends a chat-format request body (containing 'messages' field) to the completions endpoint, which rejects it with HTTP 400 'Field required: messages'. The same endpoint works fine for chat completions via curl, proving the endpoint itself is not the problem.
aliases: autocomplete role fails with self-hosted OpenAI models
signals.review_reason: Autocomplete is a core Continue feature. When the autocomplete role is assigned to an OpenAI-compatible self-hosted model, every code completion request fails with HTTP 400 because Continue sends the wrong request body format (chat-style with 'messages') to the completions endpoint. This is a persistent, reproducible workflow failure affecting self-hosted model users.

source_issues.title: ai completions for openai based self hosted endpoints is broken
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400 'Field required: messages' error from completions endpoint; curl to same endpoint works; error log shows Continue sending chat-format body (with 'messages') to the /completions endpoint, which expects a 'prompt' field. Autocomplete feature completely unusable with OpenAI-compatible self-hosted models.

signals.topic: A2A SDK 1.0+ incompatibility causes ImportError and prevents agent-to-agent communication setup
signals.summary: Users cannot use the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) feature when using a2a-sdk 1.0.1 or later — the crew fails to initialize with an ImportError before any meaningful work can begin.
signals.review_reason: Users cannot use the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) feature at all when using a2a-sdk 1.0.1 or later — the crew fails to initialize with an ImportError before any meaningful work can begin. This is a complete blocking issue for agent-to-agent communication, which is a core feature use case.

signals.summary: InternalInstructor sends requests to api.openai.com instead of the user-configured endpoint (vLLM, Ollama, etc.), breaking structured outputs for all non-OpenAI endpoints.

This is a main flow failure for structured output use cases with any non-OpenAI endpoint.

signals.review_reason: Users who pay for and rely on premium models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, Gemini 3.1) through OpenRouter cannot use them with CrewAI — the agent execution fails with an empty response error. This directly wastes user API costs and blocks their main workflow.

signals.topic: SSE /chat endpoint sends 'complete' event instead of 'error' when strategy loading fails, silently misclassifying failures as success
signals.summary: The REST /chat SSE endpoint emits a 'complete' event even when the strategy name is invalid and prompt/session construction fails, causing clients to incorrectly interpret failed requests as successful. This is a silent failure that violates the streaming contract and can lead to downstream misclassification of failures.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug: the /chat SSE endpoint is a core user interaction path. When a strategy name is invalid, the handler logs an internal error but still emits a 'complete' event, causing clients to silently misclassify failed requests as successful. This violates the SSE streaming contract and can propagate false success signals to downstream consumers. The issue has a local regression test confirming the bug, and the severity is amplified because it affects the SSE contract itself, which is the primary client-facing protocol.

source_issues.title: /chat SSE returns complete even when strategy loading fails
source_issues.evidence: SSE stream emits {"type":"complete","format":"plain","content":""} when strategy loading fails; no SSE error event is emitted; clients receive misleading success signal for failed requests

signals.topic: Ollama vendor not recognized despite correctly configured .env (DEFAULT_VENDOR, OLLAMA_BASE_URL)
signals.summary: Fabric CLI and Server fail to recognize the 'Ollama' vendor even when DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama and OLLAMA_BASE_URL are explicitly set in ~/.config/fabric/.env, returning 'could not find vendor' error during execution.
aliases: Ollama remote setup vendor mapping failure
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug on a core user workflow: users cannot use the chat or stream commands with Ollama, even with correctly configured .env settings. The vendor registration/mapping fails silently, preventing the entire chat pipeline from running. The issue shows clear user impact: the model is identified but vendor lookup fails, and the workaround requires manual ollama/ prefixing or a full reinstall. The bug was open for 17 days and required maintainer intervention to close, indicating non-trivial impact.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: "could not find vendor" error despite correctly configured .env (Ollama/Remote)
source_issues.evidence: Despite DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama and OLLAMA_BASE_URL set correctly in .env, Fabric returns 'could not find vendor'; fabric -L can list models from the remote URL (proving connectivity), but the chat/stream logic fails to map the model to the vendor; issue closed after 17 days with maintainer interaction

signals.topic: Shell command execution fails across multiple environments
signals.summary: Users cannot execute external shell commands — failures occur on RHEL (Permission denied), Windows with PowerShell 7 only (hardcoded powershell.exe), and even in YOLO mode (PowerShell prompts still block). This blocks the core use case of running system commands.

signals.review_reason: Three distinct shell execution failures across RHEL, Windows PowerShell 7, and YOLO mode — all variants of the same root cause (CLI cannot reliably invoke external shell commands). count=3 meets the threshold. The core CLI use case of running commands is blocked for multiple user segments.

source_issues.title: run_shell_command fails with Permission denied
source_issues.evidence: On RHEL8/9, all external commands fail with execvp(3) Permission denied. Works in NFS home dir and local temp. Gemini CLI is the only tool affected — main flow is completely blocked on RHEL.

source_issues.title: run_shell_command forces powershell.exe instead of pwsh.exe
source_issues.evidence: gemini-cli is hardcoded to use powershell.exe. Windows systems with only PowerShell 7 (pwsh.exe) installed cannot run shell commands at all — main flow blocked.

source_issues.title: Yolo mode still prompts for PowerShell execution
source_issues.evidence: Even with -y YOLO flag, PowerShell security prompts block execution, requiring manual confirmation. The autonomy feature is non-functional.

signals.topic: Backspace key inverts character/word deletion on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows, the Backspace key executes deleteWordLeft instead of deleteLeft, deleting entire words instead of single characters. Ctrl+Backspace behavior is also inverted. This breaks fundamental text editing muscle memory for all Windows users.
aliases: Backspace deletes whole word instead of character
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm backspace inversion on Windows. This is a main flow blocker: all text editing on Windows is broken, affecting every interaction. Count=2 meets the frequency threshold for a single-repository issue with clear blocking evidence.

source_issues.title: Backspace key inversion on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Backspace executes edit.deleteWordLeft instead of edit.deleteLeft on Windows PowerShell/CMD. Ctrl+Backspace is inverted. All Windows users affected — fundamental text input is broken.

source_issues.title: Backspace deletes whole word instead of character

Crash with ENAMETOOLONG when model hallucinates file path

source_issues.title: Unhandled ENAMETOOLONG Error When Processing JSON
source_issues.evidence: CLI crashes with ENAMETOOLONG during normal JSON data processing (API responses with email, phone, avatar fields). Crash occurs in lstat call — session dies during normal operation.

source_issues.title: Crash with ENAMETOOLONG when model hallucinates file path
source_issues.evidence: Model concatenated code to a path argument, causing lstatSync to fail with ENAMETOOLONG. Session crashes. Reporter notes it is a 'security-relevant bug causing session death.'

signals.topic: CLI auto-exits prematurely during YOLO mode autonomous tasks

signals.review_reason: Premature CLI exit during YOLO mode blocks the autonomous operation use case. Despite count=1, the behavior is clearly disruptive — user cannot complete any multi-step autonomous task. Valid pain point but single report prevents P0.

source_issues.title: Auto exiting while performing tasks
source_issues.evidence: CLI auto-exits while performing tasks in YOLO mode with terminal error. User provided screenshots showing premature exit after a few steps. The autonomous workflow cannot complete.

signals.topic: MCP environment variable expansion failure breaks Docker MCP integrations
signals.summary: The CLI passes literal ${VARIABLE_NAME} strings to MCP server args instead of expanding them from the environment, causing authentication failures for Docker-based MCP servers.
aliases: Environment Variable Expansion Failure in mcpServers Configuration
signals.review_reason: MCP integration with environment variable injection is completely broken. Docker-based MCP servers cannot authenticate. While count=1, the feature (MCP env var expansion) is a core integration capability and its failure prevents the entire MCP workflow for affected users.

source_issues.title: Environment Variable Expansion Failure in mcpServers Configuration
source_issues.evidence: MCP server configuration with ${VARIABLE_NAME} env var placeholders in args array are passed as literal strings. Docker-based MCPs receive invalid credentials (e.g., literal '${DISCORD_TOKEN}' instead of actual token), causing TokenInvalid authentication errors.

signals.topic: Tool save/export misses Python dependencies for imports with inline comments, causing incomplete requirements.txt
signals.summary: 当工具函数包含带 inline comment 的 import 语句（如 `import IPython  # noqa: F401`）时，get_imports() 用 regex 无法识别该依赖，导致 make_gradio_app 导出的 requirements.txt 缺少依赖项，工具部署后因缺依赖而失败。
aliases: Tool save misses requirements for commented imports
get_imports regex fails on commented imports
signals.review_reason: Regex-based import detection fails on inline-comment imports, leading to incomplete requirements.txt in tool export workflow. This directly breaks make_gradio_app tool deployment in a reproducible way — required runtime dependencies are silently omitted, causing downstream import errors. The issue is not theoretical: the reporter provides a concrete reproduction case with a real library (IPython). This is a workflow-runtime failure in the tool save/export pipeline, meeting the '主流程失败' and '关键功能不可用' criteria.

source_issues.title: Tool save can miss requirements for commented imports
source_issues.evidence: A function tool with an inline-comment import (import IPython  # noqa: F401) is saved with make_gradio_app=True, but the resulting requirements.txt only contains smolagents instead of also IPython. This causes tool deployments to fail due to missing runtime dependencies.

signals.topic: Codex agent stops prematurely during interactive sessions due to ignored 'never stop' instruction

signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-runtime issue where Codex integration fails the core interactive session use case. The agent halts prematurely, directly blocking users from the main feature (observing and intervening in agent work). 37 comments confirm active community impact. While only 1 issue, the severity and specificity (Codex specifically broken vs Claude working) indicate a real product deficiency rather than a one-off user error.

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: User reports Codex ignores 'never stop' instruction unlike Claude, causing agent to halt mid-session. 37 comments indicate active community discussion and confirmed usability issue. Interactive sessions (the core feature enabling users to watch agent work and pitch in) are broken for Codex users.

signals.topic: SummarizationMiddleware never trims state.messages — unbounded checkpoint growth causes OOM
