source_issues.title: SummarizationMiddleware never trims state.messages, causing unbounded checkpoint growth
source_issues.evidence: Bug report: SummarizationMiddleware never trims state.messages, causing unbounded checkpoint growth. state.messages grows without limit, eventually causing OOM/out-of-storage. Author confirmed reproducible.

source_issues.title: SummarizationMiddleware never trims state.messages, causing unbounded checkpoint growth
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report (closed) from a different author confirming the same SummarizationMiddleware unbounded growth issue. Two independent reports confirm the memory/resource leak.

source_issues.title: Silent worker crash when passing a `ChatOpenAI` instance to `create_deep_agent` under streaming (openai 2.x + deepagents 0.5.3)

signals.topic: CompositeBackend route isolation leaks across shared storage backends — data accessible across route boundaries
signals.summary: CompositeBackend does not properly isolate routes when backends share storage. Files and data written to one route can be accessed from other routes, causing data isolation failures in multi-tenant or multi-user scenarios.
aliases: Route data leaks between CompositeBackend partitions
signals.review_reason: 数据隔离失效：CompositeBackend 的路由分区之间存在数据泄露，同一存储后端的多个路由之间可以互相访问彼此的文件和数据，在多租户或多用户场景下构成严重的数据安全问题。

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend route isolation leaks across shared storage backends
source_issues.evidence: Bug report describing route isolation failure: CompositeBackend routes share storage backend state, causing files/data written in one route partition to be accessible from another route partition. Critical data isolation issue in multi-tenant agent scenarios.

signals.topic: Summarization middleware loses images in multimodal conversations
signals.summary: When using multimodal conversations with image content (e.g., screenshots, charts), the SummarizationMiddleware causes image data to be lost during the summarization offload process. Users lose image content with no recovery.
signals.review_reason: 多模态数据丢失：涉及图片内容的对话在进行摘要卸载时图片数据丢失，用户无法恢复。在需要处理图表、截图等多模态内容的 agent 场景中造成关键数据不可用。

source_issues.title: Summarization middleware image loss
source_issues.evidence: Bug report: SummarizationMiddleware causes image loss in multimodal conversations. Images (screenshots, charts) are stripped or lost during the summarization offload process. Data loss in multimodal agent workflows.

signals.topic: Duplicate tool_calls in content_blocks with OpenAI Responses API streaming
signals.summary: OpenAI Responses API streaming includes both partial fc_-prefixed blocks and final call_-prefixed blocks, causing duplicate tool_calls in content_blocks.
aliases: OpenAI Responses API streaming duplicate tool_calls
signals.review_reason: UX degradation in streaming — users receive duplicate tool_calls blocks in content_blocks, breaking the recommended serialization pattern. Affects all users of OpenAI Responses API streaming with tool calls. Two separate reports confirm the issue.

source_issues.title: Duplicate tool_calls in content_blocks with OpenAI Responses API streaming
source_issues.evidence: When using OpenAI Responses API streaming, content_blocks includes both partial fc_-prefixed blocks (empty args accumulated during streaming) AND final call_-prefixed blocks (full args). This causes serialization issues when using content_blocks, the recommended pattern.

source_issues.title: Duplicate tool_calls in content_blocks with OpenAI Responses API streaming
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #36985 — same issue filed separately.

signals.topic: _convert_openai_format_to_data_block hard-codes mime_type application/pdf on all base64 file blocks
signals.summary: All base64 file blocks get mime_type='application/pdf' regardless of actual file type (CSV, text, spreadsheets all mislabeled), propagating wrong types to downstream integrations.
signals.review_reason: Silently corrupts MIME types for non-PDF files sent via base64 format, causing downstream integrations to misinterpret file types. Affects every user sending CSV, text, or other file types through the OpenAI file block format. Two separate reports confirm widespread impact.

source_issues.title: core: _convert_openai_format_to_data_block hard-codes mime_type on base64 file blocks
source_issues.evidence: The _convert_openai_format_to_data_block function hard-codes mime_type='application/pdf' for all base64 file blocks, ignoring the actual MIME type from the data URI. CSV, text, spreadsheet files get incorrectly labeled as PDF. Since _normalize_messages calls this on every chat model input path, the wrong MIME type propagates to all downstream integrations.

source_issues.title: core: _convert_openai_format_to_data_block hard-codes mime_type=application/pdf on base64 file blocks
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #36939, closed.

signals.topic: Agent recursion limit of 9999 causes massive API cost blowout
signals.summary: Agent default recursion limit of 9999 is undocumented and causes runaway API calls, with one user reporting $800 in cost within one afternoon.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure with explicit cost impact ($800). The agent default recursion limit of 9999 is undocumented and causes uncontrolled API calls leading to massive cost loss. User provided LangSmith evidence of runaway execution. This is a clear cost-loss pain point.

source_issues.title: Agent default recursion limit is 9999, user lost $800 in one afternoon
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports $800 cost in one afternoon due to 9999 default recursion limit. The limit was changed from 10000 to 9999 but never documented. User provided LangSmith URL showing expensive runaway execution.

signals.topic: create_agent stale structured_response from checkpoint causes premature agent exit
signals.summary: When using create_agent with response_format and a checkpointer, structured_response restored from a previous checkpoint causes the agent to exit prematurely before processing new input.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking bug in create_agent — the agent exits prematurely with stale structured_response data instead of processing new input. Affects any agent using checkpointing with structured output, a core use case.

source_issues.title: create_agent: stale structured_response from checkpoint causes premature exit on next turn
source_issues.evidence: When using create_agent with response_format and a checkpointer, structured_response is restored from the previous turn's checkpoint. The routing edges use 'structured_response' in state as an exit condition, causing the agent to exit before the model runs for new input, returning stale data instead.

signals.topic: ChatAnthropic cache_creation token count reports 0 despite cache writes
signals.summary: ChatAnthropic reports cache_creation as 0 in usage_metadata even when cache is being written to, breaking cost tracking for users relying on usage_metadata.
signals.review_reason: Incorrect cost tracking — users relying on usage_metadata for cache token counts get 0 instead of actual values, leading to wrong billing calculations. Clear cost-loss impact for users monitoring cache efficiency.

source_issues.title: ChatAnthropic: usage_metadata.input_token_details.cache_creation is 0 when tokens were written to cache
source_issues.evidence: When using ChatAnthropic with cache control (ephemeral TTL), normalized usage_metadata.input_token_details.cache_creation reports 0 even though raw response_metadata.cache_creation_input_tokens and ephemeral_5m_input_tokens are both correct. This causes incorrect cost tracking for users relying on usage_metadata.

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that arrive after Overwrite in same superstep
signals.summary: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently discards values arriving after Overwrite in the same superstep with no error or warning, causing silent data loss in concurrent execution paths.
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss in channel updates is a critical correctness issue. When multiple nodes write concurrently and one writes Overwrite followed by others writing regular values, those regular values are silently discarded. In concurrent supersteps this is a common execution path, meaning user state updates are randomly lost with no indication of failure.

source_issues.title: bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: Silent data loss: values arriving after Overwrite in same superstep are silently discarded with no error or warning. Example: [Overwrite(10), 5] expected to raise InvalidUpdateError but returns 10 with 5 dropped.

source_issues.title: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that appear after an Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: Same bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() drops subsequent values after Overwrite in identical atomic time-step with no warning or error, causing silent data loss.

signals.topic: Checkpointer fork creates duplicate human messages in branched state instead of replacing
signals.summary: Forking from a checkpoint with a new human message produces duplicate messages instead of a clean branch, corrupting agent conversation history and breaking time-travel/regenerate workflows.
signals.review_reason: Forking from a checkpoint with a new human message produces duplicate messages instead of a clean branch. This corrupts agent conversation history and breaks time-travel/regenerate workflows, which are key LangGraph features for conversational AI applications.

source_issues.title: Agent with checkpointer=True: forking human message produces duplicate human messages in new branch
source_issues.evidence: Fork with checkpoint_id=<pre-human> and new input human('hi2') produces state [human('hi'), human('hi2'), ai(new)] instead of expected [human('hi2'), ai(new)]. Old human message incorrectly carried over into new branch.

signals.topic: Second consecutive regenerate from same checkpoint overwrites previous branch instead of creating new sibling
signals.summary: Regression since 1.1.7 breaks the regenerate/time-travel workflow — calling regenerate twice with the same checkpoint silently overwrites the previous branch instead of creating a third one.
signals.review_reason: Regression since 1.1.7 breaks the regenerate/time-travel workflow - a core UX feature. Calling regenerate twice with the same checkpoint silently overwrites the previous branch instead of creating a third one. User loses previous branch history without any indication of the overwrite.

source_issues.title: Regression in 1.1.7 (#7498): Second regenerate from latest checkpoint doesn't create new branch
source_issues.evidence: Regression since 1.1.7: calling astream twice with same parent checkpoint_id fails to create a second sibling branch. Third call still only shows 2 branches, with AI output silently overwriting branch 2. Bisected to PR #7498.

signals.topic: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes, bypassing retry logic on re-invocation
signals.summary: The sync path is missing a guard that the async path has. When a task fails or is interrupted with CachePolicy enabled, error writes are cached and replayed as valid results on re-invocation, completely bypassing retry logic.
signals.review_reason: When using CachePolicy with sync API, failed or interrupted task writes are cached and replayed as valid results on re-invocation. This silently bypasses retry logic - users believe their graph succeeded when it actually errored. This is a silent correctness failure that masks failures from users.

source_issues.title: bug: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes (async path already guarded)
source_issues.evidence: Sync path missing guard that async path has. When a task fails or is interrupted with CachePolicy enabled, error writes are cached. On re-invocation with same inputs, cache replays those error writes as valid results, completely bypassing retry logic and returning errors instead of re-executing.

signals.topic: langgraph-cli 0.4.21 missing typing_extensions dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments
signals.summary: The langgraph CLI crashes completely on any clean environment with ModuleNotFoundError because schemas.py imports typing_extensions.Required but the dependency is not declared.
signals.review_reason: The langgraph CLI crashes completely on any clean environment with ModuleNotFoundError. Users cannot run basic CLI commands like 'langgraph build' out of the box, blocking the entire local development workflow. This is a main flow failure on first use.

source_issues.title: langgraph-cli 0.4.21: Missing typing_extensions dependency causes ModuleNotFoundError on clean environments
source_issues.evidence: schemas.py imports typing_extensions.Required but typing_extensions is not declared in package dependencies. Clean environments like GitHub Actions runners crash with ModuleNotFoundError when running langgraph CLI commands.

signals.topic: Plugin daemon fails to initialize plugin instances in offline/intranet environments, causing installed plugins to be non-functional despite successful installation
signals.summary: Offline plugin installations complete but the plugin daemon cannot initialize plugin instances, causing 'Internal Server Error' and 'no proper instance' errors when trying to use installed plugins.
signals.review_reason: Two related issues both in offline/intranet environments: plugin installs successfully but is non-functional (#35555), and pyproject.toml-based plugin upgrades fail with context canceled (#35546). Both prevent offline/intranet plugin usage — a key enterprise deployment scenario. Count=2, single repo, different failure modes but same root domain.

source_issues.title: Plugin installed successfully offline but fails to work.
source_issues.evidence: Offline plugin installation completes successfully and plugin daemon process is healthy, but model credential configuration immediately returns Internal Server Error: 'no proper instance' / PluginDaemonInternalServerError. Plugin is installed but completely non-functional.

source_issues.title: Plugin upgrade/install fails instantly with context canceled when using uv sync (pyproject.toml)
source_issues.evidence: Plugin daemon detects pyproject.toml and attempts 'uv sync' to build virtual environment, but fails within ~78 microseconds with 'context canceled' error. Installation fails instantly.

signals.topic: Workflows with Human Input Nodes get permanently stuck in PAUSED state when accessed via Service API — no endpoint to retrieve form, submit approval, or resume workflow
signals.summary: Service API users cannot retrieve the human input form, cannot submit approval/rejection, and cannot resume workflows that pause at human approval nodes. Workflows are permanently stuck in PAUSED state.
aliases: Service API lacks Human Input Node support
signals.review_reason: Missing critical API endpoint causes production workflows to be permanently blocked at human approval nodes. Enterprise users integrating via Service API have workflows that cannot be resumed — effectively dead workflows. Main-flow blocking issue for API-based deployments.

source_issues.title: Feature Request: Service API Support for Human Input Node (Workflow Pause/Resume)
source_issues.evidence: Service API users cannot retrieve the human input form, cannot submit approval/rejection, and cannot resume the workflow. Workflows permanently stuck in PAUSED state. Enterprise automation platforms integrating via Service API cannot use Human Input Nodes in production.

signals.topic: Workflows with LLM nodes frequently hang in 'running' state with no streaming response on frontend while backend produces correct results
signals.summary: Workflows with large model nodes frequently get stuck in 'running' state indefinitely with no frontend response, even though backend execution completes correctly with valid results.
aliases: Streaming data not displayed on frontend despite backend success
signals.review_reason: Frequent intermittent workflow execution failure where LLM node hangs with no frontend output despite backend having results. User describes as 'very often failing'. Core workflow execution issue that undermines reliability.

source_issues.title: Workflows often get stuck when reaching large model nodes.
source_issues.evidence: Workflows with large model nodes get stuck in 'running' state with no response. Results are visible in backend but absent on frontend. User describes it as 'very often failing' to execute. Core workflow execution failure.

signals.topic: Manually stopped chatflow sessions incorrectly remain in 'running' status in conversation logs with zero token consumption recorded
signals.summary: When a user manually stops a chatflow response, the conversation log entry remains in 'running' state indefinitely and token usage shows as 0, creating log data integrity issues.
aliases: Conversation log shows wrong status after manual stop
Stopped sessions stuck in running state in logs
signals.review_reason: Log state inconsistency — interrupted sessions show 'running' status with zero token usage. Creates data integrity issues in the audit/log system. Non-blocking but impacts monitoring reliability.

source_issues.title: chatflows that are manually stopped by the user remain in a running state in the log system
source_issues.evidence: User presses stop response button, agent stops generating output, but conversation log entry remains in 'running' state. Token usage displays as 0 even after subsequent successful responses. Log data integrity is unreliable.

signals.topic: Workflow log cleanup configuration (WORKFLOW_LOG_CLEANUP_SPECIFIC_WORKFLOW_IDS) is completely ignored — old logs are not deleted even when config is set correctly
signals.summary: The WORKFLOW_LOG_CLEANUP_SPECIFIC_WORKFLOW_IDS environment variable has no effect. Logs are not cleaned up according to the configured retention policy, causing unintended database bloat.
aliases: Workflow log retention config not working
signals.review_reason: Documented configuration parameter for selective workflow log cleanup is completely non-functional. Leads to unintended database bloat and storage costs. Users relying on retention policies for compliance or cost control are not protected.

source_issues.title: Regarding the issue where the WORKFLOW_LOG_CLEANUP_SPECIFIC_WORKFLOW_IDS configuration parameter is not taking effect
source_issues.evidence: User configured all cleanup parameters correctly (WORKFLOW_LOG_CLEANUP_ENABLED=true, WORKFLOW_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS=3, WORKFLOW_LOG_CLEANUP_SPECIFIC_WORKFLOW_IDS). Logs older than 3 days are not deleted. Configuration is completely non-functional.

signals.topic: ADD-only v3 pipeline lacks semantic conflict resolution: contradictory facts accumulate and degrade retrieval quality
signals.summary: The v3 extraction pipeline is ADD-only: add() no longer emits UPDATE/DELETE events. When users add contradictory facts (e.g., 'I work at Company A' followed by 'I now work at Company B'), both are stored as separate ADD events. The system only does exact MD5 hash deduplication — it has no semantic comparison. This causes stale facts to surface in search results alongside current ones, degrading the accuracy of memory retrieval for time-sensitive attributes like employment, location, or relationship status.
signals.review_reason: P1: Count=3 issues all describing the same root cause — the documented 'latest truth wins' conflict resolution is unimplemented in the ADD-only pipeline. User impact is real (stale facts returned in queries, degraded retrieval accuracy), but it is a design regression rather than a hard block since search still returns results.

source_issues.title: ADD-only extraction in v3 may surface stale/contradictory facts for time-sensitive attributes
source_issues.evidence: Concrete scenario: 3-month-old 'Works at Company A' memory coexists with today's 'Works at Company B' after upgrade to v3. Retrieval returns Company A as top candidate because scoring signals don't incorporate recency.

source_issues.title: ADD-only architecture doesn't implement conflict resolution for semantically similar memories
source_issues.evidence: Code evidence in main.py: MD5 hash dedup only. Adding 'my name is Alice' then 'my name is Bob' stores both as ADD events. get_all() returns 2 results instead of 1. Documented behavior 'latest truth wins' is unimplemented.

source_issues.title: fix: semantic conflict resolution missing in v2 ADD-only pipeline
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: memory.add('my name is Alice') then memory.add('my name is Bob') → both return ADD event, get_all() returns 2 results. Root cause: no cosine similarity comparison between new and existing memory vectors. Proposed TDD fix outlined.

signals.topic: OSS REST API GET /memories breaks after v3 filter requirement: top-level entity params rejected
signals.summary: After v3 migration, get_all() rejects top-level user_id/agent_id/run_id and requires them inside a 'filters' dict. The OSS REST server's GET /memories endpoint still forwards query params as top-level kwargs, causing all such calls to fail with 'Top-level entity parameters frozenset({user_id}) are not supported in get_all(). Use filters={user_id: ...} instead.' This is a breaking API change with no migration path — existing clients and scripts break silently or with an error message. Related: DELETE /memories has the same structural issue (see pp3).
aliases: REST API breaking change v3 filter requirement
OSS REST API entity params rejected v3
signals.review_reason: P1: Breaking API change that blocks existing OSS REST API clients after v3 upgrade. Count=2 (GET /memories + proxy MemoryClient search path), both with clear reproduction steps and ValueError evidence. Not P0 because the workaround (POST /search) exists.

source_issues.title: [Bug] OSS REST GET /memories forwards top-level entity params to get_all() and fails after v3 filter requirement
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression after v3 migration. Every REST API client calling GET /memories?user_id=X breaks with a ValueError. Workaround requires switching to POST /search with filters dict.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Proxy MemoryClient search path is broken
source_issues.evidence: Proxy MemoryClient._fetch_relevant_memories passes user_id/agent_id/run_id as top-level kwargs to search() — crashes with ValueError. Additionally crashes with TypeError on dict iteration. Blocks the Mem0 proxy chat path entirely for MemoryClient users.

signals.topic: v3 migration breaks self-hosted Qdrant deployments: hardcoded threshold floor, native deps mis-bundled, history writes silently diverted
signals.summary: Three compounding bugs introduced by v3 migration make the mem0 OSS plugin silently non-functional for self-hosted Qdrant users: (1) auto-recall hook hardcodes a 0.6 score floor, ignoring user-configured searchThreshold — on text-embedding-3-small, legitimate matches scoring 0.35–0.55 are dropped silently, so auto-recall injects nothing; (2) tsup bundles better-sqlite3 native .node binary inline, breaking runtime resolution on Node versions without prebuilts — history writes are silently disabled with no warning; (3) resolvePath mangles absolute historyDbPath values, diverting writes to CWD-local memory.db instead of the configured path.
aliases: Qdrant self-host three bugs v3 migration
signals.review_reason: P0: User-visible main-flow failure (auto-recall silently returns nothing, history writes silently diverted) backed by concrete reproduction data on 19,619 real memories. All three bugs are silent — users see 'no memories returned' with no error, making diagnosis extremely painful. Count=1 but review_reason provides unambiguous strong evidence of production impact.

source_issues.title: v3 migration breaks self-host on Qdrant: auto-recall threshold ignored, history writes diverted, native deps mis-bundled
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction data on 19,619 real memories shows 0 matches above 0.6 threshold for queries 'family', 'identity', 'recent projects', 'user preferences'. SQLite silently disabled on Node 25 without prebuilt binary. Absolute historyDbPath diverted to CWD on every run. Three bugs stack — each masks the next — causing 'no memories returned' and 'entity collection stays empty despite successful adds'.

signals.topic: Concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index, causing IndexError on subsequent reads
signals.summary: When multiple coroutines concurrently call AsyncMemory.add(), AsyncMemory.update(), or AsyncMemory.delete(), Qdrant's HNSW index becomes corrupted, producing 'IndexError: index N is out of bounds for axis 0 with size M'. Subsequent reads (search, get) either return wrong results or crash until the process is restarted and the index is rebuilt. Root cause: asyncio.to_thread dispatches synchronous vector_store writes to a thread pool, and Qdrant's upsert/HNSW builder is not re-entrant — a second writer arriving while the first graph update is in-flight reads a partially-built structure.
aliases: AsyncMemory concurrent write Qdrant HNSW corruption
Qdrant HNSW index out of bounds concurrent writes
signals.review_reason: P0: Data corruption bug that blocks all subsequent reads on the affected Qdrant index, requiring process restart and index rebuild to recover. Confirmed in sustained production workloads over multiple months. Blocks core async workflow for any multi-coroutine agent.

source_issues.title: Bug: concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index ('index N is out of bounds')
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code shows 20 concurrent writers trigger reproducible corruption. Corruption was observed in sustained production workloads over several months before root cause pinpointed. Index must be rebuilt to recover.

signals.topic: REST API DELETE /memories returns misleading success message but does not delete all matching memories
signals.summary: DELETE /memories?user_id=... returns 'All relevant memories deleted' but only removes memories up to the vector-store page size limit in a single call. In the reported case, 148 memories were reduced to 48 after one DELETE — a second call was required to reach 0. This creates a data integrity hazard: callers trust the success message and never issue a second delete, leaving residual memories that should have been purged (e.g., user deletion/GDPR requests).
aliases: DELETE API incomplete deletion misleading success
REST API delete all memories pagination bug
signals.review_reason: P1: Data integrity hazard — GDPR/user deletion requests are a compliance-critical workflow where residual data after a claimed 'success' delete is a real problem. Count=1 but strong reproducible evidence and clear user impact (misleading success causing incomplete data deletion).

source_issues.title: REST API `DELETE /memories?user_id=...` does not delete all matches in one call and returns misleading success message
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible test: 148 memories → 48 after first DELETE (success message shown) → 0 after second DELETE. Caller cannot distinguish partial from complete deletion from the response.

signals.topic: .NET Workflow Sample compilation failure — missing ConfigureProtocol implementation
signals.summary: The official .NET workflow sample does not compile because it requires implementing the abstract method `ConfigureProtocol`, leaving users unable to run workflows out of the box.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking issue. The official workflow sample in the repository does not compile at all, preventing users from running and experimenting with the workflow functionality. This is a primary onboarding failure — users hit it immediately when trying the documented getting-started path.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Workflow Sample does not compile
source_issues.evidence: Sample at dotnet/samples/03-workflows/Agents/CustomAgentExecutors does not compile — abstract method ConfigureProtocol must be implemented; workflow does not run even with a naive implementation

signals.topic: Python multi-user session isolation failure in workflow-as-agent deployments
signals.summary: When deploying a workflow-as-agent behind an HTTP endpoint serving multiple users, per-user session memory is shared across users regardless of session ID, making multi-user deployments fundamentally broken.
aliases: memory shared across users in multi-user deployments
signals.review_reason: This is a critical functional gap for production multi-user deployments. The session isolation mechanism, which is the documented approach for per-user memory management, is fundamentally broken. Users cannot build a multi-tenant SaaS agent service using the framework's session API — a core production use case is blocked.

source_issues.title: Python: Session isolation does not work as expected for workflow-as-agent deployments in App Service / Container Apps
source_issues.evidence: When sharing a workflow/agent instance across multiple users with distinct session IDs, memory is shared across users. Rebuilding the workflow per request also loses memory. Neither pattern achieves isolated per-user memory and preserved session state simultaneously — a core requirement for multi-user SaaS deployments.

signals.topic: Python FoundryChatClient async context manager protocol missing — official sample fails
signals.summary: FoundryChatClient lacks `__aexit__`, causing the documented 'built-in chat clients' sample to crash with TypeError when users try to run it with the Foundry client.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow startup failure for the official sample. The sample code that ships with the framework crashes immediately on the documented Foundry client path. While there is a workaround (wrap in Agent instead), users hitting this have no clear path forward and the experience signals severe SDK quality issues.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: FoundryChatClient doesn't support async with, built_in_chat_clients sample fails
source_issues.evidence: Running the official built-in chat clients sample with foundry_chat client crashes with TypeError: FoundryChatClient object does not support the asynchronous context manager protocol (missed __aexit__ method). The sample explicitly uses 'async with client:'.

signals.topic: .NET OpenTelemetry dependency vulnerability blocks CI pipelines and local builds
signals.summary: OpenTelemetry.Api 1.15.0 has a known moderate-severity vulnerability. This version is pinned in the .NET project, breaking CI and local builds until upgraded.
aliases: CI pipeline failure due to vulnerable dependency
OpenTelemetry moderate severity vulnerability blocking builds
signals.review_reason: While the underlying vulnerability may not directly affect runtime behavior, the pinned vulnerable dependency version actively blocks CI pipelines and local builds — a significant developer experience and deployment workflow disruption. The issue explicitly states 'breaking CI pipeline and local builds', which qualifies as a cost/delay impact for any team using this .NET package.

source_issues.title: .NET: Upgrade OpenTelemetry dotnet version to 1.15.3
source_issues.evidence: OpenTelemetry.Api 1.15.0 has GHSA-g94r-2vxg-569j, a moderate severity vulnerability. This version is pinned in dotnet/Directory.Packages.props and is breaking CI pipelines and local builds. Version 1.15.3 is patched.

signals.topic: Python agent-framework-azure-ai ImportError due to BaseContextProvider version mismatch
signals.summary: Importing FoundryEvals from agent-framework-azure-ai fails with ImportError because it depends on BaseContextProvider which is not exported in agent-framework 1.1.1.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete startup/blocking failure — users cannot even import the Azure AI integration package due to a version mismatch. This blocks all users of the azure-ai evaluators feature, a documented integration path.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: ImportError: cannot import name 'BaseContextProvider' from 'agent_framework' when importing agent_framework_azure_ai
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'BaseContextProvider' from 'agent_framework' when running 'from agent_framework_azure_ai import FoundryEvals'. The azure-ai package depends on BaseContextProvider which is absent from agent-framework 1.1.1. Blocks any user trying to use Azure AI evaluators.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 以非沙盒方式执行 LLM 生成代码，存在提权与系统破解风险
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 将 LLM 生成的代码直接写入磁盘并以 subprocess 执行，无任何沙盒、文件系统隔离或网络限制。仅有初始化时的 UserWarning，可被生产配置静默吞掉。用户若部署在生产环境接收到恶意 prompt injection，可导致：任意代码执行（凭据窃取、SSH 密钥外泄、横向移动、数据销毁）。攻击路径具体可操作。
signals.review_reason: 明确的用户影响证据：生产部署时若使用 LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor（文档 quickstart 中广泛示例），遭遇间接 prompt injection 可导致任意代码执行、凭据窃取与横向移动。攻击路径具体（asyncio.create_subprocess_exec），影响严重（系统完全危害），非理论性威胁。提权至 P1 而非 P0 因 count=1 且单仓，无多用户投诉样例。

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: UserWarning 仅在初始化时触发，可被 -W ignore 或日志管道静默过滤；无运行时安全控制；攻击场景：prompt injection 诱导 LLM 生成恶意代码写入磁盘并执行，窃取 ~/.ssh/id_rsa、执行横向移动

signals.topic: Multi-agent 对话缺乏确定性 loop-breaking 机制，agent 陷入礼貌性循环时产生高额 API 账单
signals.summary: AutoGen 的 GroupChat 完全依赖 LLM 内部逻辑判断何时终止或切换状态。当两个 agent 进入礼貌性循环（'I agree', 'Thank you for the code'），框架无法感知语义进度，持续消耗 API 配额直至 max_turn 硬限制。企业用户面临 $500+ 过夜账单风险。

API credit runaway from conversational loops

signals.topic: Python Redis connector multiple bugs: vector search broken, delete silently fails, malformed FT.CREATE PREFIX
signals.summary: The Python Redis connector has three independent but co-located bugs that collectively break core vector store operations: (1) FT.SEARCH raises AttributeError due to redisvl API incompatibility, (2) RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True (data not deleted, no error raised), (3) FT.CREATE sends one prefix per character instead of one prefix per collection name (index matches unintended keys in multi-collection deployments).
signals.review_reason: Three co-located bugs in the Python Redis connector block core vector store operations. Vector search is completely broken (AttributeError on every call). Delete silently fails with data corruption (no error, record remains). Malformed FT.CREATE causes cross-collection data contamination in multi-tenant deployments. All three have concrete wire-format evidence and reproducible repro scripts. Combined they represent a systemic failure of the Redis connector's core CRUD and search paths.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Vector search (FT.SEARCH) via the Python Redis connector is broken
source_issues.evidence: FT.SEARCH raises AttributeError: 'StorageType' object has no attribute 'index' on every search call. Root cause: redisvl ~=0.4 pin resolves to 0.15.0 where API changed to require IndexSchema. No compatible redisvl version exists that satisfies both SK redis>=6 requirement and redisvl<0.5. Affects every Python user installing SK from committed uv.lock.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled
source_issues.evidence: RedisJsonCollection._inner_delete does not apply collection-name prefix to keys. JSON.DEL targets non-existent key, returns 0, record never deleted. No error raised — silent data corruption. Only manifests when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True (common pattern for multi-collection deployments).

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Redis connector sends malformed FT.CREATE PREFIX (one prefix per character of collection name)
source_issues.evidence: FT.CREATE sends PREFIX N where N=length of collection name, with each character as a separate prefix. In multi-collection deployments, indexes register overlapping single-character prefixes and can match each other's keys, causing data correctness failures. RediSearch silently accepts the malformed command, making this a silent correctness issue.

signals.topic: HITL resume 场景下混合并行工具调用（部分需审批）导致已执行工具输出被静默丢弃，触发 400 API 错误阻断主流程

signals.topic: websockets==16.x 版本约束阻止项目升级到 v0.14，依赖冲突导致被迫降级或维护独立依赖集
signals.summary: SDK v0.14 引入了非可选依赖 `websockets>=15,<16`，但 websockets 16.x 唯一 breaking change 是 Python 3.10 要求（与 SDK 自身要求相同），代码中未使用任何在新版本中有行为变化的 API。这导致依赖 websockets==16.x 的项目无法升级 SDK 或必须维护隔离的依赖集。
signals.review_reason: 依赖版本约束是实际阻塞用户升级到最新版 SDK 的问题，用户被迫做依赖隔离或降级，维护成本显著。虽然是单 issue，但影响所有想同时使用 websockets==16 和 SDK v0.14 的用户，影响面广。websockets 16.x 并非新版本，SDK 无理由的严格上限是维护问题而非 bug，降为 P1。

source_issues.title: Relax websockets<16 upper bound
source_issues.evidence: Issue 明确指出被迫在'全局降级 websockets'或'为 openai-agents 维护独立依赖集'之间二选一，属于依赖管理摩擦。同样问题也存在于 realtime 和 voice 可选依赖。

signals.topic: Async Responses structured output parsing causes unbounded memory leak due to Pydantic TypeVar schema rebuilds
signals.summary: 每次调用 responses.parse() 时，由于 TextFormatT TypeVar 无法被 Pydantic 解析，model_rebuild 始终返回 False，导致 MockCoreSchema._built_memo 未被缓存，每个请求都分配新的 SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer 重型 Rust 对象，在长运行服务中 RSS 线性增长直至 OOM。
aliases: Pydantic v2 TypeVar schema rebuild memory leak
multiprocess forkserver Pydantic model instantiation crash
signals.review_reason: 两条 issue 均证明 Pydantic v2.x TypeVar schema rebuild 缺陷导致严重的内存/稳定性问题。#3084 明确展示线性内存增长直至 OOM（长运行服务主流程阻断）；#3079 展示 forkserver 生产环境中 ~0.6-9.5% 的请求错误率（关键功能不可用）。两者根本原因相同（TypeVar schema rebuild 无法缓存），用户影响明确（崩溃、OOM、反复失败）。

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: 长运行服务中 RSS 线性随请求数增长，最终 OOM。Flame graph 证明每次 responses.parse() 调用均分配新的 SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer（重型 Rust 对象），且因 TypeVar 无法解析而无法缓存。

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: 在 ~700 个 forkserver worker 处理数百万请求的生产环境中，DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true 时约 0.6% 错误率（随时间增长），false 时约 9.5% 错误率，导致大量请求直接失败（'Pydantic models should inherit from BaseModel, BaseModel cannot be instantiated directly'）。

signals.topic: GPT-5.4-mini 模型使用图片/文件参数时 500 内部错误率高达 95%，同参数 GPT-5.4 正常
signals.summary: 使用 ResponseInputImageParam 上传图片时，gpt-5.4-mini 模型 95% 请求返回 500 内部错误并重试 3 次失败，而相同输入下 gpt-5.4 模型完全正常，导致图片输入功能对 GPT-5.4-mini 用户完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 95% 错误率 + 3 次重试全部失败 = 主流程阻断。图片输入对 GPT-5.4-mini 用户完全不可用，与同条件 GPT-5.4 对比证明是模型级别问题，阻断用户使用更小更便宜模型的关键功能。count=1 但有强用户影响证据支撑。

source_issues.title: GPT-5.4-Mini returns 500 internal errors 95% of the time when providing input files / images as parameters
source_issues.evidence: 使用 ResponseInputImageParam 带图片 URL 时，gpt-5.4-mini 每次返回 500 内部错误并自动重试 3 次全部失败；相同输入参数换用 gpt-5.4 则完全正常。关键功能（图片输入）对 gpt-5.4-mini 用户完全不可用。

signals.topic: 使用自定义 API base URL 时请求被 SDK 错误拦截，返回 'Your request was blocked'
signals.summary: 用户配置自定义 API base URL 后，所有请求均被 SDK 拦截并返回 'Your request was blocked' 错误，相同请求直接用 requests 库或 litellm 可正常发送，证明 SDK 在处理自定义端点时有额外校验或头部导致请求被误判为被阻断。
signals.review_reason: 自定义 API base 是生产部署中常见需求（Azure、代理、自托管等），SDK 对自定义端点请求的误拦截直接导致用户无法使用非官方端点，属于主流程阻断。虽有 cross-check（requests/litellm 正常），但 issue 已关闭说明厂商已知晓，保留用于反映用户影响。

source_issues.title: OpenAIException – 'Your request was blocked' with custom API base
source_issues.evidence: 使用自定义 API base URL 时所有请求均返回 'Your request was blocked'，直接用 requests 库发同一请求正常，litellm 也正常，证明 SDK 对自定义端点有额外处理导致请求被误拦截。关键功能（自定义端点接入）完全不可用。

signals.topic: Responses API 返回 output_text.text=null 时 SDK 解析失败，Response.model_validate 抛出验证错误
signals.summary: 当 Responses API 响应包含 text 字段为 null 的 output_text 项时，SDK 严格解析模式拒绝接受 null 值导致 Response.model_validate 失败；同时 responses.parse() 仍尝试对 null text 进行结构化解析，导致关键路径失败。
aliases: Response output_text null text parsing failure
null text field validation error Responses API
signals.review_reason: Responses API 的 output_text 解析是核心路径，SDK 对合法 API 响应（text=null）直接拒绝导致解析失败，属于主流程阻断。count=1 但有明确代码级复现和修复方向（已有相关 PR），影响明确。

source_issues.title: Response.output_text and responses.parse fail when an output_text item has text: null
source_issues.evidence: API 返回包含 text=null 的 output_text 项时，SDK 严格解析直接抛出验证错误拒绝接受，responses.parse() 仍对 null text 进行结构化解析失败。已有相关 PR #3062，属于 Responses API 核心解析路径失败。

signals.topic: responses.parse() 在 v2.21.0 中产生大量 PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue 序列化警告
signals.summary: 调用 responses.parse() 并指定 pydantic text_format 模型时，SDK 触发大量 PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue 警告，覆盖控制台输出且可能导致序列化结果不符合预期，影响生产环境日志和响应正确性。
signals.review_reason: 大量序列化警告虽非直接崩溃，但覆盖生产日志、暗示序列化结果不可信，影响 responses.parse() structured output 这一关键功能的可靠性。持续多版本活跃（2.21.0至今），属于明显的用户体验下降。

source_issues.title: responses.parse() throws a PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue error in v2.21.0
source_issues.evidence: responses.parse() 对每个 output 类型（ParsedResponseOutputText、ParsedResponseOutputMessage、FunctionToolCall 等十余种）均产生 PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue 警告，v2.21.0 引入，影响使用 pydantic structured output 的所有用户。

signals.topic: doctor() 报告的 details[] 字段类型声明为 string[] 但实际包含非字符串值，导致下游日志渲染为 "[object Object]"，诊断信息完全丢失
signals.summary: AcpRuntimeDoctorReport.details 类型合约被违反，details[] 中包含 Error 实例或普通对象而非字符串。下游消费者执行 details.join("; ") 时输出 "[object Object]"，用户可见日志中的诊断信息被完全破坏。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但用户影响明确且严重：诊断报告的 details[] 在用户可见日志中被渲染为无意义的 '[object Object]'，导致故障排查信息完全丢失。日志中有明确的字面量证据（openclaw 侧已确认并在消费者侧打补丁）。影响诊断能力，属于体验显著下降，符合痛点定义。

source_issues.title: doctor() violates its own type contract: details[] contains non-strings, rendered as "[object Object]" downstream
source_issues.evidence: 下游 openclaw 消费 acpx@0.5.3 时，日志中出现字面量 '[object Object]'，直接证明 non-string 从 details[] 中泄漏。openclaw 侧已在 https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/70825 添加防御性转换作为临时补丁。

signals.topic: ACP 持久会话客户端在 runTurn 结束后未归还连接池，每次 send 都重新冷启动，导致每个 turn 额外耗时 20-112 秒
signals.summary: 持久模式 ACP 会话的生命周期不对等：ensureSession 将客户端放入 pendingPersistentClients 池，但 runTurn finally 块无条件执行 client.close()，没有对称的「归还池」分支。导致每个 turn 后适配器进程退出，下一次 send 必须重新 spawn，产生完整冷启动代价（Claude ~23s，Gemini 74-112s）。
aliases: persistent ACP client torn down after every turn
cold-start every session_send instead of reusing connection
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但用户影响极其严重且有具体量化证据：所有 ACP 持久会话用户每次发送消息都承受完整冷启动代价（Claude ~23s，Gemini 74-112s）。Issue 中包含本地验证的实际 timing 数据，证明同一 PID 和 agent_started_at 在无修复时不复用。这是主流程阻断级别的问题——持久会话的核心价值（保持状态、避免冷启动）完全失效，属于 P0 的「主流程阻断+具体量化证据」情形。

source_issues.title: [bug] persistent ACP client not returned to pool after runTurn
source_issues.evidence: Issue 中包含本地验证的实际数据：turn 1 和 turn 2 使用同一 PID 104981，agent_started_at 在有修复时保持不变（无修复时产生新时间戳）。无修复时每次 turn 产生 23s（Claude）和 74-112s（Gemini）的冷启动延迟。已提供完整代码差异（manager.ts L293/L324/L519）和完整修复方案。

signals.topic: Skill security scanner produces widespread false positives, blocking distribution of legitimate skills
signals.summary: Automated security scanning (VirusTotal Code Insight, LLM moderation) incorrectly flags legitimate skills — including official vendor SDKs, financial trading APIs, cybersecurity tools, and content-generation tools — causing them to be hidden or rejected. Users cannot install flagged skills in non-interactive/CI environments without --force flag.
aliases: Skill security scan false positives — legitimate skills incorrectly flagged/suspended
VT Code Insight false positives blocking legitimate trading SDK skills
LLM moderation false positives — cultural/educational keywords misidentified as malicious
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用 + 主流程阻断：17个issue全部是合法技能（官方SDK、金融API、安全工具、内容生成工具）被自动化安全扫描错误标记为可疑/恶意，导致技能被隐藏或拒绝安装。在CI/Docker/MCP等非交互环境中，标记为可疑的技能静默安装失败，用户在不知情的情况下无法使用这些技能。

source_issues.title: False-positive VT Code Insight flags blocking installs of legitimate trading SDK skills
source_issues.evidence: 13 trading/prediction-market skills (8.3k downloads, 21 stars) blocked by VT heuristics. Non-interactive installs (CI, Docker, MCP server, agent harness) silently fail without --force flag. 'eval' false positive in code comments/variable names. Adlai88 explicitly states 'Users who don't know about --force silently can't install.'

source_issues.title: Re-evaluation request: topview-skill — emoji ZWJ false positive
source_issues.evidence: Official Topview AI Python SDK blocked by VT and LLM scanner. ZWJ unicode false positive from emoji glyph in user-facing templates. Network endpoint list needed manual audit to prove 100% on .topview.ai.

source_issues.title: Skill flagged — suspicious patterns detected (trade-router, re-bruce-wayne)
source_issues.evidence: Solana swap/limit-order API reference skill blocked. Static scanner flagged env var name, financial APIs, and WebSocket — all standard for trading-API clients. Skill has 801 downloads and human review 'Benign' verdict but remains flagged.

source_issues.title: Skill be flagged as suspicious and being marked hidden
source_issues.evidence: Cybersecurity prevention tools (pentester/Red-Team skill) permanently hidden from marketplace. Publisher explicitly states these are defensive tools, not offensive ones.

source_issues.title: Skill being flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: User submits appeal to re-evaluate skill that adds quota-footer to channel messages. Footer uses llm_output metrics, message_sending hooks, OpenAI Codex OAuth — legitimate monitoring feature flagged as suspicious.

source_issues.title: ZenQuote Skill False Positive — VirusTotal Misidentification
source_issues.evidence: ZenQuote skill (public API calls to zenquotes.io via curl) flagged by VirusTotal as 'SuspiciousCurl.EXE'. ClawHub's own scan correctly identifies it as Benign. Publisher notes 'similar skills that make API calls (weather, news, etc.) may encounter the same false positive pattern.'

source_issues.title: False Positive: Skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious (aifans4u)
source_issues.evidence: AIFans4u skill (external agent identity registration, inbox read, follow/like/comment) blocked. Publisher provides full audit confirming no malicious code, no hardcoded secrets, no data exfiltration. All high-risk actions require Owner approval.

source_issues.title: Skill flagged — suspicious patterns detected (zhanggroot7/project-explorer)
source_issues.evidence: project-explorer skill flagged and hidden from marketplace. Minimal issue body, no details on why it was flagged.

source_issues.title: False positives when environment variables suggested for security purposes
source_issues.evidence: Skills using env vars to avoid plain-text API key storage are flagged as 'risky due to environment variables sent through network.' This is the opposite of best practice — storing keys in env vars (vs hardcoding) is the security-recommended approach.

source_issues.title: aws-wechat-article-topics flagged — asking for explanation
source_issues.evidence: Publisher cannot understand why skill was flagged and asks for explanation and remediation steps. Demonstrates lack of actionable feedback in flagging system.

source_issues.title: False Positive — Liuyao Skill Flagged as Suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Traditional Chinese divination (I Ching) skill blocked. Scanner flagged cultural keywords ('divination', 'fortune telling', 'i ching', 'five elements') as malicious indicators. Publisher notes these are educational/cultural terms, not malware signals.

source_issues.title: Appeal: opsrobot skill falsely flagged as suspicious by VirusTotal
source_issues.evidence: OpenClaw observability platform installation assistant (Docker/Vagrant/Otel setup) flagged by VT due to OTEL endpoint HTTP URLs — standard observability configuration incorrectly flagged as suspicious external API calls.

source_issues.title: False Positive Malware Detection for @nimsuite/openclaw-nim-channel (neteaseim)
source_issues.evidence: Official NetEase IM (云信) channel plugin blocked with 'malicious' status. False positive from bundled NetEase IM SDK (@yxim/nim-bot) containing minified/obfuscated JS (production common), WebSocket, and file system ops — standard IM SDK patterns. Static analysis passed clean.

source_issues.title: YouTube Clipper v1.0.3 skill has been incorrectly flagged
source_issues.evidence: YouTube Clipper skill flagged as suspicious. Closed after appeal — demonstrates that legitimate skills require manual re-evaluation process to unblock.

source_issues.title: Early versions with issues cause all subsequent versions to show failed even when clean
source_issues.evidence: Publisher states skill is 'clean now' but clawhub permanently shows it as suspicious because older releases were flagged. Users see suspicious badge even on clean current version. Publisher calls it 'critical skill for any remote openclaw admin' but visibility is poisoned by historical artifacts.

source_issues.title: CLI publish flow undocumented; required openclaw.compat.pluginApi + openclaw.build.openclawVersion fields only surface on failed publish (which locks the version)
source_issues.evidence: While this is primarily a docs issue, the user also describes being forced to trial-and-error through version-burn attempts to find the required fields — a direct consequence of the false-positive/blocking system.

signals.topic: Skill detail page shows invalid `openclaw skills install` command that fails at runtime
signals.summary: Every skill detail page renders `openclaw skills install owner/slug` but the CLI rejects the owner/slug form, only accepting bare slug. All users encounter broken install commands on every skill page, blocking discovery-to-install flow silently.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：所有技能详情页渲染的安装命令在运行时失败，用户无法通过复制粘贴完成安装，这是发现到安装流程的静默阻断，影响所有技能页面。

source_issues.title: Skill detail page shows invalid `openclaw skills install` command (owner/slug rejected by CLI)
source_issues.evidence: CLI `openclaw skills install owner/slug` throws 'Invalid skill slug' at runtime. Verified root cause in CLI source: slug.includes('/') is rejected. Every skill detail page currently displays a broken command with no crash telemetry — users silently fail to install.

signals.topic: Plugin publish fails with opaque "Server Error" — no diagnostic, version-locks the attempt
signals.summary: Plugin authors hitting `npx clawhub package publish` receive a non-descriptive 'Server Error' from Convex backend with no guidance on which field is missing or why, and the failed attempt permanently burns a version number.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断且成本损失：发布者无法成功发布插件，服务器返回无用的错误信息，且失败后版本号被永久锁定，迫使作者消耗 patch 版本号来进行试错，单个错误就能浪费两个版本号。

source_issues.title: Publish plugin fails with "Server Error" (Convex A / packages:publishRelease)
source_issues.evidence: User filled all form fields correctly (display name, version, source commit, source ref, 11-file tgz) but received '[CONVEX A(packages:publishRelease)] Server Error' with no diagnostic. The failed version is permanently locked. Reproducible with any code-plugin lacking required package.json fields.

source_issues.title: CLI publish flow undocumented; required openclaw.compat.pluginApi + openclaw.build.openclawVersion fields only surface on failed publish (which locks the version)
source_issues.evidence: Publishing a code-plugin requires two undocumented package.json fields. Each missing field causes a separate failed publish, each burning a version bump. User lost 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 before finding the minimal template buried in npm install. Version-locked entries cannot be unpublished.

signals.topic: Historical scan verdicts on old skill versions permanently poison current version visibility
signals.summary: When a skill's early versions are flagged as suspicious/malicious, ClawHub continues to display the suspicious verdict on the current clean version indefinitely. There is no mechanism for publishers to clear historical scan artifacts, causing ongoing user confusion and trust loss even after the skill has been fully remediated.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：即使技能当前版本已完全清洁，历史版本的扫描结果仍被永久展示，导致用户持续看到可疑标记而放弃使用。当前版本无法通过自我修正来恢复可信度。

source_issues.title: Early versions with issues cause all subsequent versions to show failed even when clean
source_issues.evidence: Publisher explicitly states: 'My skill is clean but earlier releases weren't and clawhub has permanently marked it bad, even showing suspicious for virus too but clicking in shows it's clean.' No way to clear historical scan results. Users see suspicious badge on current clean version indefinitely.

signals.topic: Skill metadata refresh does not purge historical tags, mixing old and current tag sets on detail page
signals.summary: After re-publishing a skill to fix metadata drift, historical tags from old versions remain visible on the skill detail page alongside current tags. This creates noisy/misleading tag display that may hurt search relevance and publisher credibility.
signals.review_reason: 体验下降：技能详情页标签混乱，历史版本标签与当前版本标签混排，可能影响搜索相关性并造成用户困惑。但影响范围有限，不阻断主流程。

source_issues.title: Historical tags remain visible after metadata refresh for ip-publisher v1.0.8
source_issues.evidence: After publishing v1.0.8 with correct metadata, the detail page still renders 12+ historical tags from v1.0.1 including 'v1.0.1 ip-publisher', 'hotspot', 'wechat-draft', 'xiaohongshu-draft', etc. alongside the correct current tags. No UI control to separate historical from current tags.

signals.topic: 认证失败后重试间隔过短导致网关被限流，用户设备持续断开连接
signals.summary: 认证失败时重试间隔仅1秒且无退避，重置计数器导致网关持续收到未授权请求，最终触发rate limiter使设备无法重连，同时日志文件被大量相同错误填满。
aliases: gateway rate limiter triggered by auth failures
signals.review_reason: Issue #198是明确的用户痛点：认证失败时重试逻辑存在计数器重置bug，导致1秒间隔的无限重试循环，日志中可见数百条相同错误；网关被触发rate limiter后设备无法建立任何连接，属于主流程阻断；日志填充问题造成运维负担。虽然仅1条issue不足以达到count>=3的P0高频阈值，但错误日志模式清晰、复现场景具体、影响严重程度高，归类为P1。

source_issues.title: bug: aggressive retry loop on authentication failures triggers gateway rate limiter
source_issues.evidence: 日志显示每约1秒产生一次未授权错误，最终触发'too many failed authentication attempts'限流；重试计数器在每次认证失败后被重置，指数退避(1s→2s→4s→...→60s)从未生效；限流后每次重试均重置冷却时间，使问题持续恶化。

signals.topic: sessions.json OOM: monolithic sessions index causes gateway heap exhaustion and repeated crashes during sessions.list/chat.history polling
signals.summary: sessions.json is a single monolithic JSON file that grows unboundedly. The gateway deserializes the entire file into memory on every sessions.list and chat.history poll (every 1-3 seconds from the webchat control UI). At 31MB on disk (1,407 sessions), the deserialized graph exceeds V8 heap limits. The gateway repeatedly crashes with OOM — documented crashes at 1.6GB, 3GB, and 4.3GB heap. Response times grow from ~200ms to 4000+ms as the index grows, triggering GC pauses that culminate in crash. The only user workaround is setting NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: the gateway becomes completely unavailable due to repeated OOM crashes once sessions.json exceeds ~10MB. No automatic recovery; requires either manual heap-size bump or periodic manual session cleanup. Confirmed across multiple production deployments with different session counts and file sizes. The polling pattern guarantees the crash will occur for any long-running deployment with moderate usage.

source_issues.title: Gateway OOM crash: sessions.json (31MB / 1,407 sessions) causes heap exhaustion during every sessions.list/chat.history poll
source_issues.evidence: 31MB sessions.json, 1,407 sessions. Gateway crashes at 1.6GB (60min uptime), 3GB (5.5h), 4.3GB (9.5h). V8 Mark-Compact GC traces show allocation failures. No pagination; entire index deserialized on every poll. Only workaround: NODE_OPTIONS=max-old-space-size=8192.

source_issues.title: sessions.json parse+write blows past 60s run budget → agents silently return 'No reply from agent'
source_issues.evidence: Production: 'No reply from agent' with 60s timeout on agents with sessions.json >5MB. Operations agent: 11.7MB, 2,423 sessions, timing out. cmo agent: 18.5MB, 286 sessions, timing out. cto: 0.9MB, fine. skillsSnapshot fields total 13.2MB (71% of cmo file) — repeated identically across entries. skillsSnapshot identified as the dominant size contributor; proposed fix: content-address it out-of-line.

signals.topic: jiti plugin loader fails to resolve typebox barrel re-exports, blocking anthropic/google/lmstudio/xai/memory-core providers
signals.summary: On Node 22 + Linux, the jiti-based plugin loader cannot resolve typebox's ./else.mjs, ./el_GR.mjs, ./additionalProperties.mjs barrel re-exports. The files exist on disk and load fine with native Node ESM, but jiti's resolution fails. This makes every provider plugin that depends on typebox (anthropic, google, lmstudio, xai, memory-core — i.e. most AI providers) fail to load. The loader retries forever on a ~10-15s interval. On 2026.4.23 a secondary regression causes each retry to trigger a ~2-min merged npm install, effectively hanging the gateway. Users lose access to their primary models (Claude/Gemini).
aliases: bundled plugin loader fails typebox barrel
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: every provider plugin using typebox (anthropic, google, lmstudio, xai, memory-core — the default provider set) fails to load. 37+ error occurrences logged. No workaround exists. The jiti-vs-native-ESM resolution discrepancy means even files confirmed to exist on disk cannot be loaded through the plugin loader. Primary model usage is completely blocked.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: jiti plugin loader fails to resolve typebox barrel re-exports ('./else.mjs', './el_GR.mjs') — breaks anthropic/google/lmstudio/xai/memory-core on 2026.4.22/4.23 Linux
source_issues.evidence: 37 'Cannot find module './else.mjs'' and 30 './el_GR.mjs' errors in 7h log. anthropic, google, lmstudio, xai, memory-core all fail. Direct node import of the same files succeeds. Loader retries forever. On 4.23 each retry triggers ~2-min merged npm install, hanging the gateway.

signals.topic: Post-install runtime-deps staging self-collides with openclaw's own safety check on user-writable installs (Homebrew/macOS, nvm/pnpm)
signals.summary: On user-writable global installs (Homebrew Node on macOS, nvm, pnpm), openclaw update completes the npm install step but the post-install runtime-deps copy phase creates a staging dir (.openclaw-runtime-deps-copy-<random>) inside dist/ that openclaw's own safety check then rejects as 'Unsafe package dist path' (dot-prefixed names). The staging dir is self-cleaned on error, making it self-induced. The CLI version is updated but plugin runtime-deps are not finalized. Subsequent update invocations report 'already-current' and skip, masking the partial state forever.
aliases: dot-prefixed staging dir safety check collision
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: openclaw update fails silently on Homebrew/macOS, nvm, and pnpm — all user-writable install topologies. The CLI reports 'already-current' on every subsequent attempt, permanently masking the partial update state. Plugin runtime-deps are not finalized. This affects a broad class of non-root install methods and has no simple fix on the user side.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 'Unsafe package dist path' error from post-install runtime-deps staging (self-collision) on user-writable global installs (Homebrew Node on macOS)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed on Homebrew Node macOS arm64: openclaw update fails with 'Unsafe package dist path: dist/extensions/amazon-bedrock/.openclaw-runtime-deps-copy-KZmXaz/node_modules/.bin/fxparser'. Root-owned global installs (Linux/sudo) use ~/.openclaw/plugin-runtime-deps/ and are unaffected. Staging dir confirmed self-created and self-cleaned. Subsequent update reports 'already-current' and skips, masking the failure permanently.

signals.topic: sudo openclaw doctor --fix writes root-owned files into user ~/.npm/_cacache, breaking all subsequent non-root plugin runtime-deps installs (EACCES)
signals.summary: Running sudo --preserve-env=HOME openclaw doctor --fix (the intended invocation for root-owned installs reading user config) writes root-owned entries into the invoking user's ~/.npm/_cacache/. npm 7+ ownership safety check then fails every non-root npm call with EACCES, including the gateway's own bundled plugin runtime-deps install at startup. Every plugin depending on pi-ai/typebox/grammy/playwright-core fails validation. The gateway starts with only active-memory. The only workaround is to chown ~/.npm after every sudo doctor invocation.
aliases: plugin runtime-deps install EACCES after sudo
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: every subsequent non-root plugin install permanently fails with EACCES after the first sudo doctor run. The gateway starts with most plugins non-functional. This affects all root-owned global installs using the documented sudo doctor invocation and requires manual remediation (chown) after every sudo doctor — a maintenance burden with no automated fix.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: sudo --preserve-env=HOME openclaw doctor --fix leaves root-owned files in ~/.npm/_cacache, breaking every subsequent non-root plugin runtime-deps install (EACCES)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed on Ubuntu 24.04 + Node 24.14 + npm 11.9.0: after sudo doctor --fix, ~/.npm/_cacache/ entries are root-owned. Gateway startup fails: 'npm error code EACCES / Your cache folder contains root-owned files'. 4 plugins fail validation (browser, memory-core, memory-wiki, telegram). Only active-memory loads. Retry loop adds more root-owned entries each time. Workaround: sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.npm after each sudo doctor.

signals.topic: Subagent orphan entries (no endedAt) treated as active forever, causing main agent to hallucinate task progress in production
signals.summary: isActiveSubagentRun() treats any subagent run without endedAt as active with no staleness fallback. Any orphaned run (gateway restart mid-run, crash, kill -9, silent cron failure) never gets endedAt stamped and lives in sessions.json indefinitely. When the main agent calls subagents list to report task status, it reads these stale entries and fabricates progress narration for work that never happened — including elapsed time computations against now. Observed in production with 263 stale entries across 6 agents; the main agent told users a 'Kimi K2.6 researcher' was still running 23 minutes after the actual job died hours earlier.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking combined with hallucination of key information: the main agent fabricates task status and progress for the user based on stale data, directly eroding trust in the agent's outputs. Observed in a live production deployment. 263 stale entries in a single install confirms this accumulates silently over time and will affect every long-running deployment.

source_issues.title: [Bug] isActiveSubagentRun treats any run without endedAt as active, causing orphan entries to read as live forever (main agent hallucinates progress)
source_issues.evidence: Production evidence: 263 stale subagent entries across 6 agents in a single install. Main agent fabricated a progress report: 'Kimi K2.6 researcher — 23 minutes 44 seconds in, still researching' for a run that died hours earlier. No actual researcher had been spawned. The orphan came from a single deleted cron job (c6abfb55, hourly). Gateway restart, kill -9, and cron failures all produce orphans. No staleness cutoff exists in isActiveSubagentRun.

signals.topic: WhatsApp Dispatch 连接成功但消息无法被处理和回复（Windows 平台）
signals.summary: 用户启用 WhatsApp Dispatch 并确认连接状态为"已连接"（绿点亮起）后，发送至 Self-chat 的消息被标记为"已读"（手机端显示蓝色双勾），但桌面应用主控台无任何反应，停留在"What would you like to work on?"界面，无法执行任何操作。核心问题在于 WhatsApp Web 实例与 interpreter core 之间的数据桥接断裂。
signals.review_reason: WhatsApp Dispatch 作为关键集成功能，连接成功但完全无法处理消息，属于主流程阻断性问题。虽然只有 1 条 issue，但有明确的可复现步骤、截图证据和系统日志，证明消息读取（蓝色双勾）与 LLM 执行之间的数据传递链路断裂，用户体验显著下降。符合"主流程失败/阻断"和"体验显著下降"的痛点定义。

source_issues.title: WhatsApp Dispatch connected but not processing or sending messages windows
source_issues.evidence: WhatsApp 状态显示已连接，但用户发送消息后消息被标记为已读却无任何执行动作；主控台停留在空闲界面；bridge between WhatsApp Web instance and interpreter core is broken

signals.topic: 内置浏览器窗口遮挡所有 UI 标签页，无法切换操作
signals.summary: 在 X11 和 Wayland 两种显示协议下，用户要求 Open Interpreter 打开任何内置浏览器后，浏览器窗口覆盖所有标签页的内容区，导致用户无法切换到其他标签进行操作，应用体验完全阻断。问题在 hyprland 和 XFCE 下均可复现，非特定桌面环境问题。
