Browser z-index issue covers all tabs
signals.review_reason: 内置浏览器遮挡 UI 导致无法切换标签，属于明显的 UI 交互阻断问题，用户体验显著下降。虽然影响单一功能区域，但问题在多个桌面环境下均可稳定复现，有截图证据，7 条评论表明社区关注度较高。属于"体验显著下降"类痛点。

source_issues.title: Browser pages cover middle area of UI, regardless of what tab is selected
source_issues.evidence: 浏览器窗口遮挡所有标签页，用户无法切换操作；有截图证据；在 hyprland 和 XFCE 下均可复现；7 条评论表明问题持续存在且影响多用户

signals.topic: Git cache file corruption causes struct.error crash on startup
signals.summary: When the git cache file is corrupted or truncated, fun.py read_cache() throws struct.error: unpack requires a buffer of 8 bytes, crashing aider before any productive use. Two distinct issues with identical root cause.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：两个独立用户在不同时间遭遇同样的崩溃，app在sanity_check_repo阶段直接退出，完全无法使用。根因是.git cache文件损坏或被截断导致read_cache()中struct.unpack失败。已open状态表明尚未修复。

source_issues.title: Uncaught error in fun.py line 263
source_issues.evidence: struct.error: unpack requires a buffer of 8 bytes at read_cache() in fun.py line 263; appelsZijnCool reports on Linux, crash occurs during sanity_check_repo -> get_tracked_files -> _deserialize -> read_cache

source_issues.title: Uncaught error in fun.py line 263
source_issues.evidence: Identical struct.error crash, second user report on same platform (Linux), same stack trace. Both issues open.

signals.topic: Git config lock file blocks aider startup
signals.summary: Aider fails to start when a stale git config.lock file exists, raising an uncaught OSError that prevents any productive use.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：aider在setup_git阶段即退出，错误信息要求用户手动删除.git/config.lock文件。这对普通用户构成显著的体验下降和流程阻断，特别是当锁文件由其他进程遗留时。已open状态表明尚未修复。

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1045
source_issues.evidence: OSError: Lock for file '.git/config' did already exist; occurs at setup_git -> config_writer -> _acquire_lock -> _obtain_lock_or_raise; crashes before any coding can begin

signals.topic: Missing playwright module causes crash when using /web or URL scraping
signals.summary: When a user tries to scrape a URL via the /web command, aider crashes with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright', requiring manual extra installation.
signals.review_reason: 工作流阻断：用户在尝试使用/web命令抓取URL内容时直接崩溃。playwright作为可选依赖未被默认安装，但import时没有优雅降级而是直接抛出ModuleNotFoundError，导致整个check_for_urls流程失败。用户体验显著下降。

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in scrape.py line 144
source_issues.evidence: User attempts to use URL scraping via check_for_urls -> cmd_web -> scraper.scrape() -> scrape_with_playwright(); import playwright fails; crash blocks the web scraping workflow on Windows 11 with CPython 3.12

signals.topic: Analytics module TypeError crashes aider on launch
signals.summary: Aider crashes immediately on launch due to a TypeError in analytics.py where Client.capture() receives multiple values for distinct_id, blocking all usage.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：analytics.event()在main()启动阶段即被调用，TypeError导致整个app无法启动。这是aider核心遥测代码的bug，而非用户配置问题，影响所有使用该代码路径的用户。

source_issues.title: Uncaught TypeError in analytics.py line 240
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Client.capture() got multiple values for argument 'distinct_id' at analytics.event('launched') in main.py; crash occurs before any coding interaction begins on macOS with virtual environment

signals.topic: Julia file causes tree-sitter QueryError crash in repo map
signals.summary: When a repo contains Julia source files, aider crashes during repo map generation with a tree-sitter QueryError: Invalid node type, preventing any productive use of the tool on Julia projects.
signals.review_reason: 工作流阻断：用户在Julia项目中与aider交互时，repo map生成阶段的tree-sitter查询因Julia语法解析器节点类型不匹配而崩溃，导致整个coding session中断。此问题在#4867中持续open，存在超过50天，表明Julia用户长期受影响。

source_issues.title: Julia crashes aider
source_issues.evidence: tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module; crash occurs in get_tags_raw -> _run_captures(Query(language, query_scm), tree.root_node); user can create Julia file but subsequent interaction crashes the repo map on Linux with Gentoo

signals.topic: UI and SQLite persist plain-text API credentials including Authorization headers, causing credential leakage on copy-paste
signals.summary: promptfoo's UI Details panel and ~/.promptfoo/promptfoo.db store provider configs verbatim, including rendered Authorization: Bearer tokens and API keys. Users sharing debug Details blobs or exports leak live credentials without realizing it. Anyone with machine access retrieves every credential ever used.
aliases: API key exposure in eval records
plain-text Authorization header in UI details
signals.review_reason: This is a direct credential leak where users unknowingly expose live API keys/tokens when sharing debug output. The user's own credential is at risk, and the blast radius is silent and broad — affecting all eval exports, shared eval URLs, SQLite history, and UI copy-paste actions. Severity is elevated because users are unaware of the leak until damage is done. P0 despite count=1 because the impact mechanism (credential exfiltration) is severe and the affected code path is triggered by every eval run.

source_issues.title: UI and stored eval record expose rendered Authorization / apiKey in plain text
source_issues.evidence: User reports that opening the UI Details panel and copying/pasting the Provider section leaks rendered Authorization: Bearer <live_token>. The same value is stored verbatim in ~/.promptfoo/promptfoo.db SQLite. Author categorizes impact as 'medium-high' — the user is the victim and does not see the risk until the credential is already shared.

signals.topic: OpenRouter provider hardcodes apiBaseUrl, silently overriding user-supplied proxy/custom endpoint
signals.summary: OpenRouterProvider spreads user config but then overwrites apiBaseUrl with the hardcoded 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1' URL last. Any user-supplied apiBaseUrl in promptfooconfig.yaml is silently discarded, causing all requests to go to the default endpoint even when a compliance gateway, caching proxy, or fork is intended.
signals.review_reason: Main eval flow is silently broken for a legitimate and common enterprise use case (routing OpenRouter traffic through a proxy). The user gets no error, no warning — requests simply go to the wrong endpoint, typically surfacing as an unexpected 401 from the proxy. This is a complete workflow blocker for proxy-based setups, and P0 despite count=1 because the root cause is a one-line code bug with a known fix, and the impact is silent failure of the primary request path.

source_issues.title: openrouter provider: hardcoded apiBaseUrl silently overrides user config
source_issues.evidence: Bug report includes verified source code reference showing the hardcoded apiBaseUrl overwrites user config via spread order. Reproducible by setting apiBaseUrl in yaml config — requests go to default endpoint with no error or warning. Common enterprise use case (compliance gateway, internal proxy) is completely broken.

signals.topic: YAML config params silently ignored when declared in wrong section (assert/provider vs defaultTest/options/provider)
signals.summary: When a user declares provider config in both defaultTest.options.provider and assert.provider, the assert-level config is silently ignored. There is no warning or error log when promptfoo silently discards yaml configuration params, leading to unexpected provider behavior and difficult debugging.
aliases: no warning for ignored yaml params
signals.review_reason: This is a configuration UX failure where promptfoo silently discards user-provided yaml params without any warning. Users waste significant debugging time (author notes it was 'quite hard to debug'). While count=1, the underlying pattern (silent config discarding) is a systemic UX issue that likely affects more users. Marked P1 (not P0) because the immediate failure is for a non-core feature (LLM judge config), not the primary eval flow.

source_issues.title: Improve Documentation: OpenAI compatible API
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'It was unclear to me how to define the judge endpoint and ended up declaring the full config in the defaultTest/options/provider but also adding this id in the assert/provider. As a result my config was silently ignored and I could only set the url and apikey through global var env.' User explicitly requests: 'promptfoo warn in its logs when some params of the yaml config are ignored.'

signals.topic: Thinking-capable self-hosted LLM judges fail JSON parsing with confusing error, requiring obscure showThinking:false workaround
signals.summary: When using self-hosted OpenAI-compatible LLMs (e.g., vLLM) with thinking/reasoning capability as LLM judges, promptfoo attempts to parse thinking tokens as JSON content, causing 'Could not parse Json' or 'string' errors. The workaround (adding showThinking:false) is undocumented and hard to discover — promptfoo does not display the string it was trying to parse.
aliases: vLLM thinking model judge parsing error
signals.review_reason: This breaks the LLM-as-judge assertion flow for any user running self-hosted thinking-capable models (a growing and common deployment pattern with vLLM, Ollama, etc.). The error message is uninformative ('Could not parse Json' with no context) and the fix is undocumented. Count=1 but the affected model category (all thinking-enabled self-hosted models) is broad. P1 because it blocks evaluation completion for a legitimate and increasingly common judge setup.

source_issues.title: Improve Documentation: OpenAI compatible API
source_issues.evidence: User reports that with a vLLM judge model having thinking capability, promptfoo 'will try to parse the json starting with the thinking content, which most often leads to errors ("string" or "Could not parse Json"). This was quite hard to debug since promptfoo doesn't show the string it was trying to parse.' Author notes this is likely 'un-noticed since the official openai API doesn't output thinking tokens' — meaning all self-hosted thinking models are affected.

signals.topic: llm-rubric assertions in defaultTest cannot resolve template variables, making shared rubrics non-functional
signals.summary: When an llm-rubric assertion is defined in defaultTest (shared across test cases), template variables like {{input}} and {{myVar}} are not resolved — the rubric receives the literal string '{{myVar}}' instead of the actual test case variable value. This makes defaultTest-level rubric assertions fundamentally broken for any rubric that needs to reference per-case input.
aliases: llm-rubric template variables not resolved in defaultTest
signals.review_reason: This is a core feature break for the defaultTest sharing mechanism — one of the primary ways promptfoo enables DRY test configuration. Rubrics silently receive wrong input (unresolved template strings), and some models grade these as 'correct' making the wrong behavior invisible. Users cannot use the intended design pattern (shared rubric in defaultTest referencing per-case vars) at all. P0 despite count=1 because it completely breaks a core architectural pattern for a widespread use case.

source_issues.title: llm-rubric assertions in defaultTest cannot access test case variables via {{varName}} template syntax
source_issues.evidence: User provides full reproduction: defaultTest defines llm-rubric with '{{myVar}}' in rubric value, test_cases.yaml defines vars.myVar='hello world'. The rubric receives literal '{{myVar}}' unresolved. Author notes 'some models just grade with correct, making it hard to spot this behavior' — meaning results are silently wrong. The workaround requires a complex transform injection, which is not a reasonable expectation for users.

signals.topic: Node.hash with MetadataMode.ALL causes silent unnecessary re-embeds on file metadata changes
signals.summary: Since PR #18303, Node.hash includes all metadata fields via MetadataMode.ALL, ignoring excluded_embed_metadata_keys. Volatile file-stat fields (last_modified_date, creation_date, etc.) baked in by SimpleDirectoryReader cause hash mismatches on every cross-day file modification, silently triggering full re-embed of byte-identical content at every scheduled ingestion run. This generates direct API billing costs scaling linearly with corpus size and modification frequency.
aliases: unnecessary re-embed on file metadata change
Node.hash includes volatile file-stat metadata causing cache misses
signals.review_reason: Clear, directly measurable cost impact: unchanged file content re-embeds on every cross-day ingestion cycle, wasting API calls and billing. No warning or log emitted. Affects any production pipeline using scheduled SimpleDirectoryReader ingestion. Confirmed with reproducible script; not theoretical.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Node.hash uses MetadataMode.ALL, causing unnecessary re-embeds when volatile file-stat metadata changes
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script shows embed call count doubles after a single `touch` on an unchanged file. Demonstrates concrete wasted embed API calls. Contributor provides 5-level progressive evidence repo at github.com/stirelli/llamaindex-embedding-churn including billed-cost confirmation via real OpenAI API key. Bug confirmed in llama-index-core==0.14.21, introduced in PR #18303.

signals.topic: IngestionPipeline with num_workers > 1 silently discards all cache writes, causing repeated expensive transformation calls
signals.summary: When IngestionPipeline runs with multiple workers, cache entries written inside worker processes are lost because the in-memory SimpleKVStore is not merged back into the parent process. Subsequent multi-worker runs re-execute all transformations (including expensive embedding calls) that were expected to be cached, silently wasting compute and API costs.
aliases: IngestionPipeline cache silently broken with parallel workers
signals.review_reason: Direct data loss of cache entries: subsequent multi-worker runs re-execute all cached transformations (including embedding calls), wasting compute and API credits. Silent failure with no warning. Reproducer shows cache_size=0 vs expected cache_size=1 for identical multi-worker runs. Any user relying on IngestionPipeline caching with num_workers>1 is affected.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: IngestionPipeline with `num_workers > 1` silently loses all cache writes
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script shows sequential cache size=1 after 2 runs (cache hits work), but multi-worker cache size=0 after both runs (all cache writes silently lost). Confirmed in llama-index-core==0.14.19. Root cause identified: worker processes mutate their own in-memory cache copy which is not merged back to parent process.

signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever ignores retriever_weights in reciprocal_rerank mode, silently applying equal weights
signals.summary: When QueryFusionRetriever is configured with mode=RECIPROCAL_RANK and explicit retriever_weights, the weights are silently ignored. All retrievers contribute equally to fused scores regardless of the weights passed. This silently produces incorrect ranking results, breaking the documented API contract of retriever_weights.
signals.review_reason: API contract violation: retriever_weights parameter is silently ignored in reciprocal_rerank mode, producing incorrect fused results. No error or warning raised. Any user relying on weighted fusion ranking gets wrong results. Simple reproduction confirms expected vs actual output divergence. Direct impact on retrieval quality.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: QueryFusionRetriever ignores `retriever_weights` when `mode="reciprocal_rerank"`
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script with two mock retrievers and retriever_weights=[1.0, 0.0] returns ['node_A', 'node_C'] instead of expected ['node_A', 'node_B']. Second retriever contributes results despite 0.0 weight. Bug introduced in PR #11667 which added retriever_weights support but did not update _reciprocal_rerank_fusion(). Confirmed in 0.14.21.

signals.topic: TreeSelectLeafRetriever query path always returns empty source_nodes, breaking citations and provenance
signals.summary: TreeSelectLeafRetriever._query() returns Response objects with source_nodes=[], discarding all retrieval provenance. This breaks citation features, source attribution, evaluation/debug workflows, and any downstream code that relies on response.source_nodes to trace where answers originated. The code has an inline TODO comment acknowledging the missing fix.
aliases: source_nodes empty in tree leaf query path
signals.review_reason: Key feature (source attribution/citation) is broken for the tree-select leaf query path. Users cannot trace where answers came from, breaking evaluation, debugging, and citation workflows. Verified with reproduction script. Not blocking but significantly degrades core RAG functionality.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: TreeSelectLeafRetriever query path returns empty source_nodes
source_issues.evidence: Minimal reproduction script confirms source_nodes=[] for TreeSelectLeafRetriever._query(). The retriever traverses real leaf nodes and synthesizes an answer, but explicitly discards all source references. Inline TODO in source code acknowledges the known issue. Affects citation features, evaluation pipelines, and any downstream integration expecting source attribution.

signals.topic: LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() mutates ChatResponse.raw in-place, corrupting structured LLM responses when telemetry is active
signals.summary: When LlamaIndexOpenTelemetry (or any OpenTelemetry/dispatcher subscriber) is registered, LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() converts ChatResponse.raw from a Pydantic model to a plain dict in-place. Any code that called structured_llm.achat() and holds a reference to the response gets a corrupted object: raw is a dict instead of the expected BaseModel instance, causing AttributeError on field access. The bug is silent without telemetry and only manifests in production environments with observability enabled.
aliases: telemetry in-place mutation breaks structured output
signals.review_reason: Production-breaking bug: structured LLM output (BaseModel instances) silently corrupted to plain dicts when telemetry is enabled, causing AttributeError crashes in caller's code. Real production error traceback included. The bug is insidious because it only manifests under specific telemetry conditions, making it hard to debug.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() mutates ChatResponse.raw in-place, corrupting caller's response object
source_issues.evidence: Production error log shows AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'ruleset_id' when using StructuredLLM with LlamaIndexOpenTelemetry registered. Root cause: model_dump() mutates self.response.raw in-place rather than serializing a copy. Reproduction script shows output.raw type changes from Pydantic model to dict after model_dump() is called by the telemetry subscriber. Affects any production system using structured LLM output with observability enabled.

signals.topic: Windows: daemon start fails silently and daemon status misreports due to `ps -o pid` incompatibility
signals.summary: Two issues (#1635, #1633) document that `ps -o pid` (Unix syntax) is not supported on Windows Git Bash/msys2, causing `daemon start` to silently die after 2s and `daemon status` to always report STOPPED regardless of actual daemon state. Users cannot start or reliably monitor the daemon on Windows.
aliases: ps -o pid not supported on Windows
signals.review_reason: Two independent user reports (#1635, #1633) with distinct repro steps confirm the same root cause: `ps -o pid` Unix syntax fails on Windows Git Bash/msys2. Issue #1635 shows daemon start silently dies (main flow failure); issue #1633 shows daemon status misreports STOPPED (monitoring broken). Together they block the entire daemon lifecycle on Windows, a primary platform. No workaround for daemon start beyond --foreground flag.

source_issues.title: daemon start silently dies on Windows due to ps -o incompatibility
source_issues.evidence: On Windows Git Bash, `daemon start` reports '[OK] Daemon started' but exits within ~2s. PID file orphaned. Confirmed on both v3.5.7 and v3.5.80.

source_issues.title: Daemon status shows STOPPED on Windows — ps -o pid command not supported
source_issues.evidence: `ruflo daemon status` reports 'Status: STOPPED' immediately after starting even though process is running. Error: 'ps: unknown option -- o'.

signals.topic: Daemon state write-race: background daemon flush overwrites CLI-trigger runCount increments
signals.summary: When a background daemon periodically flushes its in-memory state to daemon-state.json and a CLI trigger concurrently executes a worker, the background flush overwrites the CLI's incremented runCount, causing persisted state to regress while real-time probes show the increment. Operators relying on persisted state see misleading 'worker did not run' when it actually did.
aliases: background daemon clobbers CLI trigger state
runCount regression due to concurrent writes

P1 (not P0) because while impactful, the work still executes — only the persisted record is corrupted.

signals.topic: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch and workflow_run report fabricated completion without routing to daemon
signals.summary: The MCP tool hooks_worker-dispatch returns status:'completed' synchronously without invoking the daemon's worker pipeline, so runCount never increments. Similarly workflow_run returns agentsSpawned:0 and validated status for both dryRun and live invocations. The CLI process workers --action list also returns hardcoded demo IDs instead of the real worker registry. Only daemon trigger --worker executes real work — the other three surfaces are stubbed.
aliases: MCP worker dispatch does not execute real workers
process workers list returns hardcoded demo IDs
workflow_run reports zero agentsSpawned on live runs
signals.review_reason: MCP surface-family defect where three separate surfaces (hooks_worker-dispatch, workflow_run, process workers list) all return fabricated/misleading results without connecting to the actual working daemon pipeline. Users trust the 'completed' status but no work is done. Clear evidence with concrete repro showing runCount unchanged after dispatch call. This is a false-positive workflow result — the user believes work completed when it did not.

source_issues.title: MCP hooks_worker-dispatch returns fabricated completion independent of daemon; process workers --action list returns hardcoded demo IDs

signals.topic: MCP artifact handlers create duplicate artifact directories under Claude Code CWD drift
signals.summary: MCP handlers use process.cwd() as artifact anchor, but Claude Code's Bash tool CWD drifts into subdirectories mid-session. Handlers invoked from subdirectories create orphan .swarm/ and .claude-flow/ artifact folders alongside the real project root, producing duplicate artifact records that poison future decisions and confuse users expecting one artifact folder per project.
aliases: Claude Code CWD drift causes artifact sprawl
MCP handlers create orphan artifact records
signals.review_reason: CWD drift in Claude Code causes artifact folders to proliferate in unintended subdirectories, producing orphan records that mislead future decisions. Documented with real-world multi-folder accumulation example. While impactful (corrupts artifact state), it is not a hard workflow block — the daemon still runs, just with corrupted data. P2 because count=1 and the core workflow continues, though decision quality degrades.

signals.topic: One-shot CLI commands (ruflo status, ruflo --version) hang ~2min before exit; AgentDB Patch warnings leak on every invocation
signals.summary: Two bugs in the ruflo wrapper: (1) one-shot commands hang for ~2 minutes before exiting because the wrapper lacks process.exit(0) on success — only has .catch(), no .then() — leaving the process alive until Node event loop times out; (2) AgentDB Patch console.warn suppression shim is bypassed in the wrapper, so [AgentDB Patch] warnings print on every command including --version.
aliases: process doesn't exit after one-shot commands
AgentDB Patch warnings leak on every ruflo command
signals.review_reason: Two bugs in the ruflo wrapper: (1) process hang blocks scripts/CI that call one-shot commands and wait for exit, with 2min delay being a significant UX and workflow degradation; (2) AgentDB Patch warning leaks on every command including --version, a persistent noisy annoyance. Both bugs are in the ruflo wrapper that bypasses already-fixed canonical CLI code. P1 not P0: count=1, though the impact (hanging scripts/CI) is real.

source_issues.evidence: ruflo status outputs correctly then hangs for ~120s. AgentDB Patch warning 'Controller index not found' appears on every invocation including --version. Verified on ruflo@3.5.80, Windows 11, Node 24.14.1.

signals.topic: open command hangs/times out on pages with reCAPTCHA or similar scripts that block load event
signals.summary: The `open` command waits indefinitely for the page `load` event, which never fires on sites using Google reCAPTCHA (or similar anti-bot scripts). This blocks browser automation on a large fraction of real-world websites.
aliases: open command hangs on reCAPTCHA pages
signals.review_reason: Confirmed main-flow blocking bug: the `open` command hangs indefinitely on reCAPTCHA-protected sites, which constitute a significant fraction of real-world web pages. The page loads correctly but agent-browser never completes the command, blocking the entire automation workflow. Reproduction is clear with a real URL, and the issue is closed with a confirmed root cause (hardcoded load-event wait).

source_issues.title: open command times out on pages with reCAPTCHA (waits for load event that never fires)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug. `open` command hangs indefinitely on reCAPTCHA-protected sites. The page loads successfully (visible in CDP targets) but agent-browser's open command never resolves. Workaround requires bypassing the open command entirely and launching Chrome directly with CLI args. Affected on both ARM64 and x86_64.

signals.topic: state load command fails with 'Resource temporarily unavailable' error in latest version — regression
signals.summary: Loading a previously saved browser state (cookies/session) with `state load` fails with 'Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)' in the latest version, despite working in earlier versions. Breaks session persistence workflows.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression from the latest version: `state load` breaks for saved browser sessions, making login cookie restoration impossible. This is explicitly marked as a regression by the user ('did not exist in earlier versions') and directly breaks a core workflow — saving and restoring authenticated sessions. The error message 'Resource temporarily unavailable' with daemon busy/unresponsive suggests a daemon concurrency or locking bug introduced in a recent release.

source_issues.title: Executing the command agent-browser state load login.json takes a long time with no response and eventually fails?
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression. User saved login cookies via `state save`, then `state load` hangs indefinitely and fails with 'Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35) (after 5 retries - daemon may be busy or unresponsive)'. User explicitly states 'This issue did not exist in earlier versions; it fails directly in the latest version.' Reproduction steps are complete with a real login flow.

signals.topic: Windows: open command reports success but get url/snapshot remain on about:blank
signals.summary: On Windows, after `agent-browser open` reports success and the browser visually navigates to the target URL, `get url` and `snapshot` still return 'about:blank' or empty content. Causes session/tab state mismatch.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed Windows-specific bug: commands report success but subsequent read commands return incorrect state (about:blank instead of actual URL). This is a critical state synchronization issue that makes the browser appear to work (success messages) while silently returning wrong data — breaking agent workflows that rely on `get url` or `snapshot` output for decision-making. Platform-specific (Windows only), with clear reproduction steps and root cause analysis provided.

source_issues.title: Windows: agent-browser connect/open succeeds but get url / snapshot still stay on about:blank or an empty page
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug on Windows with complete reproduction steps. `agent-browser open https://example.com` reports success and the real browser window visually navigates correctly, but `get url` returns 'about:blank' and `snapshot -c` returns empty content. User identifies root cause as 'session / active-page / tab-state mismatch on Windows'. Affects core read commands (get url, snapshot) which return false state after navigation.

signals.topic: --args flag incorrectly splits Chrome flags whose values contain commas (e.g. --disable-features=A,B,C)
signals.summary: The `--args` CLI flag splits on every comma, breaking Chrome feature flags that use comma-separated values inside a single flag. This prevents passing critical flags like --disable-features, --enable-features, and blocks Chrome HTTPS-first behavior.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed parsing bug with verified root cause: `--args` splits on every comma, which breaks Chromium's standard feature flag format (comma-delimited lists). This prevents passing any --disable-features or --enable-features flag correctly — a very common use case for browser automation. The bug is subtle (appears to work for simple cases) but silently fails for the most important Chromium flags. Three-way verification (source, raw Chrome, patch) makes this high confidence.

source_issues.title: `--args` incorrectly splits single Chrome flags whose values contain commas
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with verified root cause in `cli/src/main.rs`. The `--args` parser splits on every comma, turning `--disable-features=HttpsUpgrades,HttpsFirstModeV2,HttpsFirstModeV2ForEngagedSites` into multiple broken args. This breaks Chrome HTTPS-upgrade behavior needed for local dev environments. Verified by: (1) source code analysis, (2) raw Chrome works with same flags, (3) patched parser fixes the issue. Complete reproduction with auth URL flow provided.

signals.topic: Headless mode: redirect links and new tab creation don't work
signals.summary: When running in headless mode (without --headed flag), redirect-based links that open in new tabs are not captured. New tabs from redirects don't show up in `agent-browser tab` output, and agent focus doesn't shift to new tabs. Works correctly in headed mode.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed headless-specific regression: redirect links and new tab creation work correctly in headed mode but are broken in headless mode. This is a significant functional gap since headless mode is the primary mode for automated/CI environments. Users relying on headless automation will have broken workflows on sites using redirect-based navigation.

source_issues.title: Redirects don't work or new tabs don't show up when agent-browser is used in headless mode
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed headless-specific bug. In headless mode, links that use redirects to open new tabs are not captured (don't appear in `agent-browser tab` output). In headed mode, redirects work correctly and agent focus shifts to the new tab automatically. This is a headless vs headed behavioral divergence that directly breaks headless automation for redirect-heavy sites.

signals.topic: xAI/Grok tool calling fails due to `additionalProperties: false` schema conflict
signals.summary: The AI SDK unconditionally adds `additionalProperties: false` to all tool schemas. xAI/Grok explicitly rejects this field in its validator, causing every tool call against xAI models to fail with a 400 API error. No provider-specific override exists, forcing users to disable tool calling entirely for xAI.
aliases: xAI Grok tool_config schema validation failure
signals.review_reason: Primary tool-calling workflow is completely blocked for all xAI/Grok users. Every tool call fails at the API level with a 400 rejection. Count=1 but explicit API error + blocking of core workflow + documented upstream incompatibility + no partial workaround = P0.

source_issues.title: addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema breaks xAI/Grok tool calling: xAI rejects additionalProperties: false
source_issues.evidence: Every tool call against xAI/Grok fails with: '[xAI] Invalid request content: Schema validation failed: [standard_violation] /properties/properties/additionalProperties: property schema false is not supported'. Direct usage, OpenRouter routing, and any OpenAI-compatible provider routing to xAI are all affected. Users must disable tool calling entirely as workaround.

signals.topic: Audio transcription fails due to incorrect media type detection for m4a/mp4 files
signals.summary: The `experimental_transcribe` function mis-detects m4a/mp4 files as WAV because it looks for the `ftyp` box header at byte offset 0, but m4a/mp4 files prefix `ftyp` with a 4-byte box-length header (making it start at offset 4). The SDK silently falls back to `audio/wav`, causing OpenAI to reject the request with HTTP 400.
aliases: transcribe m4a ftyp offset detection failure
audio file type sniffer wrong byte offset
signals.review_reason: Transcription workflow is completely broken for any m4a/mp4 input, silently substituting an incorrect media type and causing a 400 API rejection. Byte-offset detection error is unambiguous; bypass via manual mediaType proves root cause. Affects all iOS/Android/ffmpeg/ElevenLabs recordings used as audio input.

source_issues.title: experimental_transcribe mis-detects m4a/mp4 files and sends them to OpenAI as audio/wav
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows `ftyp` at offset 4 (not 0) for all m4a files. API call to OpenAI returns HTTP 400 with 'This model does not support the format you provided.' When `mediaType: audio/mp4` is passed manually (bypassing the sniffer), transcription succeeds. Affected sources: iOS AVAudioRecorder, Android AAC encoder, ffmpeg AAC, ElevenLabs TTS m4a export.

signals.topic: Google Vertex requests fail with invalid URL when location is set to 'global'
signals.summary: When `createVertex` is configured with `location: 'global'` (required for gemini-3.1-pro-preview and other global-region models), the SDK constructs an invalid hostname by prepending 'global-' as a subdomain prefix, producing `global-aiplatform.googleapis.com` which does not exist. The request fails with a DNS ENOTFOUND error.
aliases: google-vertex global region URL construction bug
signals.review_reason: The URL construction bug makes a specific location value ('global') completely unusable, blocking access to gemini-3.1-pro-preview and other global-region Vertex models. DNS failure is deterministic and reproducible. Workaround of manual baseURL confirms correct endpoint exists when the correct URL is used.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google-vertex: Broken URL generated when using location: global (Required for gemini-3.1-pro-preview)
source_issues.evidence: The bug is in the URL construction code: it generates `https://global-aiplatform.googleapis.com/...` which does not exist. The correct global endpoint is `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/...` (no region prefix). Workaround of manually overriding baseURL proves the endpoint is reachable when the correct URL is used. Blocks access to gemini-3.1-pro-preview and any other global-requiring Vertex model.

signals.topic: useChat resume duplicates text and reasoning UI parts on stream replay
signals.summary: When `resumeStream` replays a buffered UIMessageStream against an assistant message already persisted from a previous attempt (e.g., via resumable-stream + Redis after a network blip or proxy timeout), the `text-start` and `reasoning-start` event handlers push duplicate parts rather than reusing existing ones. This causes visible UI flicker and duplicate content.
signals.review_reason: UI state corruption on resume is a main-flow degradation for any production use of resumable streams (Redis, etc.). The bug is localized, deterministic, and includes a failing test case showing duplicate parts. User-visible flicker and duplicate content on network blips directly degrade the core chat UX.

source_issues.title: useChat resume duplicates text and reasoning parts when replaying UIMessage stream
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in `createStreamingUIMessageState`: it adopts `lastMessage` but clears `activeTextParts`/`activeReasoningParts`, causing subsequent `text-start`/`reasoning-start` events to always create new parts instead of reusing existing ones. Reproduction test included with expected/actual counts. The `data-*` handler already dedupes by chunk.id but text/reasoning parts lack equivalent path.

signals.topic: UIMessagePart input-streaming types incompatible with TypeScript exactOptionalPropertyTypes
signals.summary: Under TypeScript's `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` compiler option, the `input-streaming` variants of `UIToolInvocation` and `DynamicToolUIPart` use `input: T | undefined` (required key, undefined allowed) which is not interchangeable with `input?: T` (optional key). This causes TypeScript compilation errors in pipelines using tRPC, Zod inference, or JSON utility types that erase the distinction.
signals.review_reason: Breaks TypeScript compilation for any consumer using `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` (common in strict monorepos). The type system is internally inconsistent with its own validator. This is a P1 rather than P0 because the runtime works correctly; only the type layer is broken, affecting build-time rather than run-time.

source_issues.title: UIMessagePart input-streaming types are incompatible with exactOptionalPropertyTypes
source_issues.evidence: Minimal reproduction shows `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` + tRPC/Zod inference causes TS2375 error on assignment. The Zod validator already treats `input` as optional for input-streaming states, but the TypeScript types are stricter than the runtime validator. Messages accepted by the validator cannot be assigned back into the types they came from.

signals.topic: router.refresh() eagerly refetches all in-viewport <Link> components in Next.js v16, causing ~50–200x surge in ISR Writes and massive Vercel bandwidth costs
signals.summary: After upgrading from v15 to v16, router.refresh() changed behavior — instead of marking prefetched links as stale but not refetching until user intent, it now eagerly refetches every in-viewport prefetched <Link> immediately. This caused Sanity.io's daily ISR Writes to balloon from 7.1M to 358.5M (~50x), with single-day peaks reaching 1.52B (~200x), directly driving up Vercel bandwidth and ISR costs.
aliases: ISR Write count explosion after v15 to v16 upgrade
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（router.refresh 导致 ISR 写次数暴增 50–200 倍）且产生明确计费损失，属于高优先级 P0。ISR Writes 直接关联 Vercel 平台计费，用户（SaaS 运营商）面临显著成本膨胀。有明确生产环境数据支撑，置信度高。

source_issues.title: router.refresh() eagerly refetches every in-viewport <Link> in v16 (was lazy in v15) — ~200x peak ISR Writes in production
source_issues.evidence: Daily average ISR Writes jumped from 7.1M (v15) to 358.5M (v16) — a ~50x increase; peak single-day reached 1.52B ISR Writes (~200x). In v15 behavior, prefetched Links were marked stale but not refetched until user intent. In v16, every in-viewport prefetched link is refetched immediately on router.refresh(), directly inflating ISR write counts and incurring significant Vercel bandwidth cost.

source_issues.evidence: Turbopack throws 'Global CSS cannot be imported from files other than your Custom <App>' on pages/_app.tsx even though _app.tsx IS the custom app. The error only triggers when importing BOTH a global CSS file AND next/font — removing either makes the build pass. signals.topic: use-cache stale-while-revalidate on Node runtime blocks indefinitely and never serves stale responses due to await on ignoredStream.cancel()
signals.summary: On Node.js runtime, the use-cache stale-while-revalidate mechanism never serves stale responses — it blocks on full background regeneration. Root cause: await ignoredStream.cancel() in use-cache-wrapper.ts combined with Node's Web Streams tee semantics where cancelling one branch waits until the source stream closes. This defeats the entire purpose of stale-while-revalidate caching, causing response latency spikes.
aliases: use-cache never serves stale on Node runtime
signals.review_reason: use-cache 是 Next.js 16 的核心缓存 API，stale-while-revalidate 的核心价值在于快速返回旧数据同时后台更新。Node runtime 上完全无法服务 stale 意味着缓存机制在该运行时下完全失效，导致所有 use-cache 用户的请求延迟显著增加，是核心功能的运行时回归。

source_issues.title: use-cache: await ignoredStream.cancel() blocks SWR on Node runtime (waits for source close)
source_issues.evidence: On Node runtime, use-cache stale-while-revalidate never serves stale — it blocks on full background regeneration. Root cause identified: await ignoredStream.cancel() in use-cache-wrapper.ts combined with Node's Web Streams tee semantics where cancelling one branch waits until the source stream closes, defeating the stale-while-revalidate contract. Proposed fix: void ignoredStream.cancel().catch(() => {}).

signals.topic: Graceful shutdown fails on Windows (PowerShell/CMD/sh) — long-running tasks killed without cleanup
signals.summary: When using the default shell on Windows (PowerShell, CMD, or sh via script-shell=sh), Turbo does not forward SIGINT to child tasks. The graceful shutdown sequence never fires; processes are killed immediately. This is a main-flow blocking issue for users running `turbo dev` or `turbo start` on Windows.

signals.review_reason: Two separate reports from the same user on the same day demonstrate a clear main-flow blocking issue: on Windows with default shells (PowerShell/CMD/sh), turbo kill -9 equivalents happen immediately instead of graceful SIGINT forwarding. Long-running dev servers and start tasks are forcibly killed with no cleanup, blocking the core use case of running `turbo dev/start`. This is not a niche edge case — it affects all Windows users who are the primary demographic for this bug.

source_issues.title: Graceful shutdown does not work on Windows (PowerShell / CMD)
source_issues.evidence: On PowerShell, process exits immediately on Ctrl+C: tasks killed with no graceful shutdown. Parent process exits before child cleanup completes. User shows explicit before/after comparison with bash where graceful shutdown works.

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` is not forwarded properly when `script-shell=sh`

signals.topic: `turbo affected` fails to resolve base branch in GitHub Actions — forces all tasks to run
signals.summary: In GitHub Actions CI environments, `turbo affected` cannot resolve the base branch ('main') because only `origin/main` exists in the shallow checkout. The command falls back to assuming all files changed, causing all tasks to run regardless of what the PR actually modified. This defeats the primary purpose of the affected-graph feature in CI.
aliases: affected fails to resolve main branch in CI
turbo query affected assumes all changed in CI
signals.review_reason: The `turbo affected` feature is a core CI integration for monorepo teams. When it fails to resolve the base branch, it silently degrades to assuming all tasks are affected, defeating the entire purpose of incremental CI. Users pay for and wait on full builds when only a subset of tasks should run. Two reports spanning from 2024 to 2026 show this is a persistent, recurring issue affecting production CI pipelines.

source_issues.title: `affected` failing to resolve main branch in GitHub action
source_issues.evidence: GitHub Actions log shows: 'Failed to resolve base ref main from GitHub Actions event: fatal ambiguous argument main: unknown revision'. Turbo then assumes all files changed and reports all tasks as affected, even though only one package changed in the PR.

source_issues.title: `--affected` failing to resolve `main` even on full checkout

signals.topic: pnpm 11 multi-document YAML lockfile causes workspace resolution failure and task errors
signals.summary: When pnpm 11 writes a lockfile with multi-document YAML (introduced by `configDependencies` or `packageExtensions` features), Turbo's lockfile parser throws 'deserializing from YAML containing more than one document is not supported'. This causes workspace resolution to fail and leads to task-level errors including 'Cannot find module' for pnpmfile hooks.
signals.review_reason: This blocks users from adopting pnpm 11 entirely when using turbo, since the lockfile parser cannot handle multi-document YAML. The failure cascades: workspace resolution fails, then task-level pnpmfile hooks fail, causing task errors. The user provides a clear reproduction showing `pnpm -r run typecheck` (without turbo) works fine, isolating the issue to turbo's parser. This is a blocking compatibility issue for pnpm 11 early adopters.

source_issues.title: Turbo cannot parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with multi-document YAML (configDependencies)
source_issues.evidence: User shows explicit error: 'Could not resolve workspaces: Unable to convert to yaml: deserializing from YAML containing more than one document is not supported'. Tasks fail because pnpmfile hooks can't be resolved. User explicitly notes `pnpm -r run typecheck` works without turbo, proving this is a turbo regression blocking pnpm 11 adoption.

signals.topic: Cache miss after deleting output files — cache invalidation too aggressive
signals.summary: After a successful cached build, deleting output files from the filesystem and re-running `turbo build` results in a cache miss instead of a cache hit. Turbo re-executes tasks that should have been considered cached, defeating the core value proposition of remote caching.
aliases: turbo cache miss after rm output
output file deletion causes cache invalidation
signals.review_reason: The primary value of turbo's caching is avoiding redundant builds. When a user deletes output files (a common workflow for cleanup or to force re-extraction), turbo incorrectly treats this as a cache miss and re-executes the full task. This causes unexpected CI time and compute costs, and breaks the mental model that turbo is the source of truth for what was built, not the filesystem.

source_issues.title: Cache miss after deleting output files
source_issues.evidence: User shows exact reproduction: (1) first build, (2) second build hits cache (FULL TURBO), (3) delete output dir `rm -r apps/nuxt/.output`, (4) third build shows cache MISS and rebuilds. Expected behavior: since source files and lockfiles haven't changed, the cached artifact should be re-extracted from .turbo/cache/xxx.tar.zst.

signals.topic: Peer dependencies incorrectly treated as workspace dependencies — causes unnecessary task graph branches and builds
signals.summary: When a workspace has a concrete npm dependency AND a peer dependency pointing to the same package name (pointing to a workspace), Turbo incorrectly includes the workspace in the dependency graph. This causes extra packages to be built unnecessarily and deviates from Yarn Berry's expected behavior.
aliases: peer dep treated as workspace dep incorrect graph
Yarn peer dependency workspace resolution incorrect
signals.review_reason: While this causes incorrect task graphs and wasted builds, the impact is primarily extra build time for unrelated packages rather than complete workflow failure. The bug is well-scoped (specific Yarn Berry scenario) and has a clear regression point. Classified as P2 due to count=1 and non-blocking nature, but still a meaningful user pain point causing unnecessary CI builds.

source_issues.title: Turborepo incorrectly viewing as peer deps as workspace dependencies when concrete npm dependency exists
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows that with both a concrete npm devDependency and a peer dependency to a same-named workspace, Turbo builds both the workspace and extra dependent packages that Yarn Berry would skip. The user identifies a specific commit (9deb87b) as the root cause, and notes the bug first appeared in 2.8.11-canary.2.

signals.topic: Go build fails with `go mod vendor` due to builder ignoring vendored dependencies
signals.summary: When deploying a Go project that uses `go mod vendor`, the Vercel builder ignores the vendor directory and attempts to run `go mod tidy`, which fails because it cannot access private GitHub repos. This completely blocks deployment.
signals.review_reason: This is a deployment-blocking issue. Go projects using `go mod vendor` cannot deploy at all — the builder attempts to download deps via `go mod tidy` instead of using the existing vendor directory, causing a complete build failure. The issue is labeled 'triaged: bug' and the root cause (builder not checking vendor/modules.txt) is clearly identified.

source_issues.title: Can't get vercel to deploy a `go mod vendor`-ed project
source_issues.evidence: Deployment process fails to detect vendor directory and attempts `go mod tidy`, which fails with repo access error on private GitHub library. User explicitly states deployment 'is not' buildable despite vendored deps being present in the project repo.

signals.topic: Next.js 16 post-build validation ENOENT with multi-segment Root Directory
signals.summary: When a Vercel project has a multi-segment Root Directory (e.g., `clients/admin-ui`) with a custom Build Command, Next.js 16's post-build validation computes expected file paths using only the basename, dropping intermediate segments, causing ENOENT errors on files that exist at the correct location.
aliases: post-build validation wrong file paths monorepo
signals.review_reason: This is a deployment-blocking issue for monorepo users. Next.js 16 deployments with multi-segment Root Directory and custom Build Command fail at the post-build validation step with ENOENT errors, even though the build itself completes successfully. The user's monorepo deployment is completely blocked — they had to resort to a symlink workaround.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory
source_issues.evidence: Deployment fails with ENOENT errors after 'Build Completed' step. The validator looks for files at `/vercel/path0/admin-ui/...` but files exist at `/vercel/path0/clients/admin-ui/...`. The `clients/` segment is dropped. Build itself succeeds but deployment is blocked by post-build validation.

signals.topic: `vercel redeploy` ignores `VERCEL_ORG_ID` env var, causes auth error in CI/CD pipelines
signals.summary: Unlike `vercel list` and other CLI commands, `vercel redeploy` does not call `getLinkedProject` to honour `VERCEL_ORG_ID` / `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` environment variables. This causes an auth error when the provided token is scoped to a different team than the one implied by the deployment URL.
signals.review_reason: This is a CI/CD workflow blocker. When `VERCEL_ORG_ID` is set for multi-team token management in CI pipelines, `vercel redeploy` fails with an auth error while `vercel list` works correctly. This breaks automated deployment pipelines that rely on redeploy, creating an inconsistent and unusable workflow for team-based token setups.

source_issues.title: Inconsistent cli flow between `list` and `redeploy` with env vars `VERCEL_ORG_ID`
source_issues.evidence: User gets 'Not authorized: Trying to access resource under scope X. You must re-authenticate to this scope or use a token with access to this scope' error when running `vercel redeploy` with `VERCEL_ORG_ID` set. The root cause is confirmed: `redeploy` doesn't call `getLinkedProject`, instead resolves team from token rather than project env vars. Has 1 comment confirming the analysis.

signals.topic: @vercel/oidc CJS shim breaks esbuild bundling, renders Vercel Gateway unusable
signals.summary: The @vercel/oidc package is shipped as a CommonJS shim. esbuild does not inline require statements, keeping them in the output, which causes compilation errors. This affects users embedding ai-sdk with Vercel Gateway, making it unusable in their bundler setup without manual stubbing.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional incompatibility that prevents a core product (Vercel Gateway) from working in common bundler setups. The CJS-only distribution of @vercel/oidc breaks esbuild, a widely-used bundler. Users are forced to manually stub the package as a workaround, effectively disabling Vercel Gateway functionality.

source_issues.title: CJS shim for @vercel/oidc breaks compiling
source_issues.evidence: User embeds ai-sdk which instantiates Vercel Gateway as a side effect, pulling in @vercel/oidc. esbuild keeps require statements as-is in output instead of bundling them, causing compilation failure. User has to stub out @vercel/oidc as a workaround, meaning Vercel Gateway is effectively unusable by default.

signals.topic: CLI `vercel --prod` deployments no longer include Git commit metadata (regression)
signals.summary: Deployments triggered via `vercel --prod` no longer include Git commit metadata in the dashboard — instead of showing the commit message, the dashboard only shows 'Source: vercel deploy'. This is a regression that started 2–3 days ago, breaking audit trails and deployment traceability.
aliases: CLI deploy git commit metadata missing
vercel deploy source shows vercel deploy instead of commit
signals.review_reason: This is a clear regression: CLI-triggered deployments previously showed Git commit metadata in the dashboard and now show only 'vercel deploy'. This breaks critical developer workflows around deployment audit trails, changelog generation, and traceability. The user has confirmed git metadata is present on disk, indicating the issue is on Vercel's side.

source_issues.title: CLI deploy (`vercel --prod`) no longer includes Git commit metadata
source_issues.evidence: User reports deployments succeed but dashboard shows 'Source: vercel deploy' instead of Git commit message. Git metadata is confirmed present and accessible on disk. User identifies this as a regression starting ~2-3 days ago with no config changes on their end. Has 1 comment indicating further discussion.

signals.topic: Git worktree popup 操作错误：切换 worktree 时整个项目被替换而非仅切换 worktree，或无法列出任何 worktree
signals.summary: Git worktree popup 在两种场景下均无法正常工作：1) 切换到 worktree 时整个项目名被替换成 worktree 名，且声称在 main worktree；2) 在项目根目录打开时 popup 列表为空，但 git 命令行工具正常返回 worktree 列表。用户无法通过 UI 切换 worktree。
signals.review_reason: Git worktree 是 Zed 重要的工作流功能，两个 issue 从不同角度描述了同一功能失效：worktree popup 要么显示空白列表（用户完全无法切换），要么切换后项目状态错误（误导性 UI 状态）。Count=2，根因相同（git worktree 解析逻辑错误），影响用户日常多分支开发流程。

source_issues.title: git: worktree popup switches the whole project instead of the worktree
source_issues.evidence: Using git:worktree popup to switch to feature-a worktree causes Zed to rename the entire project to 'feature a' and incorrectly report being on the 'main' worktree. Project name should remain 'monty', worktree should be 'feature-a'.

source_issues.title: git: worktree popup lists no worktrees when opened in the project root
source_issues.evidence: git:worktree popup lists no worktrees when opened in the project root (parent of .bare directory). git worktree list returns correct results in the same directory. User must manually run zed --existing to force Zed into the correct branch.

signals.topic: Agent 发送超过模型上下文窗口的 prompt，导致 API 反复拒绝请求，用户无法正常完成对话
signals.summary: Zed Agent 在长对话中未强制执行模型 token 上限，持续向 API 发送超出限制的 payload（1.5M+ tokens vs 1M 上限），API 返回错误后 Zed 又重复发送相同的超大 payload，形成死循环，用户体验极差且主流程完全阻断。
aliases: context window limit enforcement for agent
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Agent 对话在长会话场景下完全不可用，重复发送相同超限 payload 导致死循环，属于核心功能失效。Issue #54835 提供了完整的错误日志和根因分析，user impact 证据充分（反复 API 拒绝、无法继续对话）。关联 issue #49617（UI token 上限显示不准确）进一步证实系统性缺陷。

source_issues.title: Agent should prevent sending prompts that exceed model context window
source_issues.evidence: With Amazon Bedrock and allow_extended_context:true, Zed sends 1.5M+ tokens against 1M limit, gets rejected, then retries the same oversized payload repeatedly. No user signal until error appears. Error: 'prompt is too long: 1581464 tokens > 1000000 maximum'. User has no recourse other than manually starting a new thread.

signals.topic: Zed 编辑器整体变慢，自最新 Agent 更新后主流程完全不可用
signals.summary: 用户在安装最新 Agent 相关更新后，Zed 整体变得极其缓慢，用户无法与编辑器正常交互，无法工作，主流程被完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: 用户明确表示无法工作（'I cannot work'），整体应用变慢属于主流程阻断性体验下降。Review reason 中用户表述了强烈的负面影响和挫败感。注意：仅单条报告，但用户体验描述非常严重（'omega slow'，无法交互），且有版本关联（v0.233.9），按 P1 处理而非 P0。

source_issues.title: Zed is slow from the last updates
source_issues.evidence: User reports 'Zed is omega slow' since the new 'agent update'. Cannot interact with zed because the whole app is slow. User states 'I cannot work' and 'it is really frustrating to not have a properly working IDE'. Affects Zed 0.233.9.

signals.topic: ACP Agent 在 ask 模式下不显示待审批命令内容及 agent 解释，导致用户无法在执行前审查 AI 指令
signals.summary: 当 agent 的 bash tool 权限设为 ask 时，用户发起需要执行命令的请求后，UI 界面不显示实际要执行的命令内容，也不显示 agent 对该命令的说明，用户必须在不了解具体操作的情况下盲目批准，存在严重安全风险。
aliases: ACP agent command approval not showing command
ask mode bash tool command hidden
signals.review_reason: Ask 审批模式的核心理念是让用户在执行前审查 AI 指令，但当前实现在 ask 模式下完全隐藏了命令内容和 agent 解释，使审批机制形同虚设。用户无法做出知情的审批决定，属于安全攸关的功能缺陷和 UX 双重问题。

source_issues.title: OpenCode ACP Agent doesn't show the command for approval
source_issues.evidence: When agent has 'ask' permission for bash tool, and user asks it to run a command (e.g. ls), the UI shows no actual command and no agent explanation for why it needs to run it. User screenshot shows blank approval dialog. This means users must blindly approve AI commands they cannot inspect, creating a security risk for an approval workflow.
